At the same time, the astrologer says, Venus is not only about love. It also represents money, values, and our desire to possess.
Therefore, make sure that the desire to gain more does not turn into greed, an obsession with profit, or unjustified financial risk. In mundane astrology, this square may intensify issues involving large sums of money, struggles for resources and spheres of influence, sanctions, financial pressure, hidden economic interests, and corruption. The emergence of prominent information about non-transparent financial agreements cannot be ruled out

This week, not only the question of who wants what may become important, but also what price they are willing to pay for what they want
Mercury-Saturn: Reaching an agreement will not be easy
Ksenia Bazylenko also emphasized that in the second half of the week, Mercury in Libra forms an opposition to Saturn in Aries. According to her, on a personal level this may complicate negotiations and communication. Responses may be delayed, documents may require additional approval, and people may become more categorical and less willing to make concessions.
Therefore, check documents more carefully, leave extra time for important matters, and do not try to obtain an immediate response at any cost
She added that this aspect may be especially noticeable for Libras and Aries, again depending on the individual horoscope.
In mundane astrology, Mercury is associated with negotiations, information, documents, transport, and trade, while Saturn is associated with borders and restrictions. Therefore, difficult international negotiations, tough conditions, delays in reaching agreements, as well as logistical problems may arise: delays or restrictions at borders, in ports, and on maritime and other important transport routes. Achieving a quick compromise where the parties have already adopted principled positions will not be easy
What the stars foretell for Ukraine
For Ukraine, the week looks extremely eventful. According to my calculations, the opposition of Mercury and Saturn creates a tense configuration with Neptune and the Black Moon in the XII house of Ukraine’s horoscope. And this is a very interesting combination for the information space. The XII house is associated with what happens behind the scenes: secrets, closed processes, and hidden information. Therefore, there may be many scandals this week. Documents, investigations, high-profile statements, or information about what was previously being concealed may emerge. This may particularly concern government structures and officials. But Neptune has another side—confusion, manipulation, and disinformation. Therefore, not every loud sensation will necessarily prove to be true. Check your sources
The expert considers the square of transiting Jupiter to natal Pluto to be even more important for Ukraine.
Jupiter is currently moving through the seventh house of Ukraine’s horoscope—the sphere of international partners, alliances, agreements, and open adversaries. Pluto is located in the ninth house and, in the system I use, is also connected with the tenth house—state power and leadership. This may indicate a serious international situation surrounding Ukraine, tough negotiations, a clash of interests, or strong pressure surrounding an important political decision

World faces information warfare without rules — GFCN chief
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:40:37 UTC
17:40:37 KST

MOSCOW, September 13. /TASS/. Information warfare is being waged without rules, making basic fact-checking skills essential to personal safety, Vladimir Tabak, president of the Global Fact-Checking Network (GFCN), told TASS ahead of the Dialogue about Fakes 4.0 forum.
Conventional warfare is governed by established rules, he noted, and violations are referred to "a regulatory body that considers sanctions or other consequences." Information warfare has no comparable framework, he said. "Is inducing a teenager to commit murder or arson as part of information warfare equivalent to using cluster munitions in an armed conflict?" Tabak asked. "I believe it is. That goes beyond information confrontation as I understand it."
"Even when we are talking about ourselves and our opponents in this information war, there must be certain rules. Unfortunately, those rules have yet to be defined," he said. "Every adult should have at least basic fact-checking skills to protect themselves in everyday life."
Global rules: difficult but necessary
Tabak described agreement on global rules for information warfare as a difficult but necessary step.
"We understand the geopolitical situation, particularly if we were to propose them ourselves. Nevertheless, I believe these rules must be established. That is the next step," he said.
Fact-checking is no longer "a purely journalistic discipline," he added. Professional skills are also needed by "ordinary people working for private companies or the state, or independently as investigators or in related fields."
Journalism’s changing role
Despite its growing popularity, fact-checking has yet to become firmly embedded in journalism, Tabak said.
"For all the interest and hype surrounding fact-checking, it has not yet become a fundamental part of journalism," he said.
"We must also recognize how much journalism has changed. As a graduate of Moscow State University’s journalism faculty, I can say that the profession today is entirely different from what it was even 15 years ago. Many major publications are now wondering how to survive: today’s media consumption habits and the revenue models they generate seem to leave little room for news outlets of their scale," Tabak said. "The question, then, is not simply how fact-checking will fit into journalism, but what will become of journalism itself in the coming years."
GFCN
The Global Fact-Checking Network brings together experts and fact-checking organizations worldwide. Founded by the TASS news agency, the nonprofit organization Dialogue Regions and the New Media Workshop, the association works to combat disinformation. More than 125 journalists from 55 countries already collaborate with GFCN on fact-checking.
The international Dialogue about Fakes 4.0 forum will take place on September 22 at the Russia National Center in Moscow. TASS is the event’s strategic partner.

Voting under way in Sweden election that could see far right in government
The far-right Sweden Democrats party could enter government for the first time if right-wing bloc wins.
Voters in Sweden are heading to the polls in an extremely close general election that will see either the far right enter government for the first time or the centre-left opposition reclaim power.
Opposition leader Magdalena Andersson of the Social Democrats was among the first to cast her ballot after polling stations opened at 8:00am (06:00 GMT) on Sunday.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Sweden heads to the polls: What’s at stake in the knife-edge election?
- list 2 of 39/11 at 25: How the ‘War on Terror’ helped mainstream Europe’s far right
- list 3 of 3As Sweden heads to polls, Israel and Palestine policies are on the ballot
The 59-year-old, who in 2021 became the first woman to serve as Sweden’s prime minister, voted with her husband at a school in her home municipality of Nacka, south of Stockholm.
Pre-election opinion polls have long credited the four parties in her left-wing bloc with a comfortable lead over conservative Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s four-party alliance, which includes the far-right Sweden Democrats.
But the gap narrowed significantly in the final days of the campaign.
“It is now up to the Swedish people to decide which direction our country should take. Should we have a government entirely dominated by the Sweden Democrats? Something that has never happened in Sweden before? Or should we have a government led by me, which will steer Sweden in a new spirit of cooperation?” Andersson told reporters after voting.
Her party has pledged to boost the welfare state and help struggling households cope with the rising cost of living.
Kristersson aims for second term
Outgoing Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson is seeking a second four-year term at the helm of the European Union nation.
He has led Sweden since 2022 with a three-party centre-right coalition. It relies on outside support from the Sweden Democrats, an anti-immigration, far-right party that has moved towards the political mainstream, for a parliamentary majority.
If the right-wing bloc is re-elected, the Sweden Democrats can expect Cabinet posts in the next government.
Kristersson has promised to focus on improving Swedes’ everyday lives, following his government’s clampdown on organised crime and immigration.
“We want to use our new and far better preconditions to improve the lives of ordinary people … to make Sweden great again,” Kristersson told news agency AFP before the vote.
The Sweden Democrats, a party with neo-Nazi roots, took 20.5 percent of the vote in the 2022 election to become the biggest party on the right.
Kristersson announced in April that his conservative Moderates would allow the party into government if the right has a majority – though he would remain prime minister even if the Sweden Democrats are the stronger party.
Voting stations close at 8:00pm (18:00 GMT) when exit polls are expected to be published, with the first reliable results expected several hours later.
Some eight million people are eligible to vote in the election, in a country of 10.6 million where voter turnout regularly tops 80 percent.
About half of voters have cast their ballots in advance.

In Nizhnekamsk, situated roughly 1,200 kilometers from the Ukrainian frontier, residents reported low-flying unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) overhead followed by a series of heavy blasts and anti-aircraft artillery fire near the industrial district, according to independent Russian outlet Astra and Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+.

Local officials acknowledged an incident within the industrial zone, with regional official Radmir Belyaev confirming an ignition “at one of the city’s enterprises,” widely reported by monitoring groups to be Tatneft’s TANECO refining complex.
Nizhnekamsk houses one of the Russian Federation’s most critical fuel and chemical manufacturing hubs. The complex includes Tatneft’s TANECO facility, ranked among Russia’s five largest oil refineries with an annual crude processing capacity exceeding 16 million metric tons, alongside the adjacent TAIF-NK refinery, which processes more than 7 million tons of crude petroleum and gas condensate annually.
The industrial hub also hosts Nizhnekamskneftekhim, a Sibur subsidiary and one of Europe’s largest synthetic rubber and polymer producers, which holds a dominant domestic market share in synthetic rubber and industrial plastics utilized across civilian and defense manufacturing sectors.

Concurrently, overnight drone attacks struck the Slavyansk-on-Kuban oil refinery in Russia’s southern Krasnodar Krai, triggering a blaze at the facility, Astra reported.
Geolocated video footage published by local residents on social media showed a large fire and an orange glow illuminating the night sky above the plant. Regional authorities have not released an official assessment of the structural damage or casualties.
The Slavyansk refinery, operated by Slavyansk ECO, has an annual processing capacity of approximately 4 million tons of crude oil. The facility had previously halted processing operations following Ukrainian drone strikes in late April and June that caused fires in the plant’s atmospheric distillation units.
Subsequently, the Main Intelligence Directorate of the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine (HUR) confirmed that operators from the Department of Active Operations and the Department of Unmanned Systems of the Main Intelligence Directorate, as part of a joint deep-strike operation with the Ukrainian Defense Forces, struck the “Slavyansk-ECO” oil refinery in the city of Slov ’yansk-on-Kuban in the Krasnodar Krai.
“As a result of the operation, a key oil refining facility and the company’s tank farm – which fuel the criminal war against Ukraine – were struck,” HUR stated.
Thick smoke and the glow from the major fire at the Russian oil refinery are visible from dozens of kilometers away.
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine also reported that units of the Ukrainian Defense Forces struck the “Slavyansky” oil refinery in Slavyansk-on-Kuban, Krasnodar Krai, and the “Taneco” oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Republic of Tatarstan, as well as command posts and storage facilities for the Russian invaders’ attack drones.
Expanding campaign against Russian energy and chemical sectors
The overnight strikes in Tatarstan and Krasnodar Krai follow an intensified campaign by Ukrainian forces against Russian defense manufacturing, fuel distribution networks, and chemical plants over the weekend.
On Saturday, Sept. 12, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukrainian forces struck two major chemical industry enterprises in Russia’s Samara and Perm regions, alongside targets in the Black Sea and occupied territories.
In the Samara region, overnight drone strikes on Saturday ignited a blaze at the KuibyshevAzot chemical facility in Tolyatti, which produces roughly 50% of Russia’s caprolactam and 75% of its industrial tire cord.
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine subsequently confirmed a direct strike on the nearby Tolyattikauchuk plant, which produces synthetic rubbers, monomers, and high-octane gasoline additives essential for manufacturing solid rocket fuel used in tactical and ballistic missiles.
In the Perm region, long-range drones targeted the Azot plant in Berezniki on Friday, Sept. 11, which manufactures nitric acid and ammonium nitrate – critical industrial precursors for military-grade explosives.
Simultaneously, the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) conducted an operation against five military and logistics installations in Taganrog, Rostov region, striking a first-person-view (FPV) drone production workshop, two UAV warehouses, an oil storage tank, a P-18 radar station, and a Pantsir-S2 air defense system.
Ukrainian long-range drones have targeted Russian oil refineries over 70 times since early 2026, significantly reducing domestic fuel output and compelling at least 17 Russian regions to introduce fuel sales rationing.

Swiss athlete Audrey Werro has secured another victory, this time at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest.

In the process, she set several meeting records and a personal best. With a time of 1:53.70 in Zurich, she was just 42 hundredths of a second off the world record set by Jarmila Kratochvilova, which the Czech athlete had established in 1983.

“It may as well happen now,” he ventured as he met Irish prime minister Micheal Martin in Dublin, prompting pushback from pro-U.K. loyalists in Northern Ireland and some leading politicians in mainland Britain.
“Donald Trump is Donald Trump and the president will say and speak his mind as he sees it,” U.K. minister 
Angela Rayner told Sky News yesterday.
“But look, we’re really serious about the Good Friday Agreement,” she added, referring to the 1998 peace accords that largely ended three decades of sectarian conflict in Northern Ireland.
It stipulates that a referendum on Irish unity can be held if the U.K. government determines a majority there is likely in favor. Republic of Ireland voters would also need to back it in a separate poll.
Within hours of his surprise intervention on the issue, Trump had touched down in Doonbeg, on the country’s west coast, where his Trump Organization-owned golf course was hosting the Irish Open.
The American leader attended the tournament yesterday, the main reason for the trip, before departing for Washington later in the day.
Martin assured him at Saturday’s meeting that Doonbeg’s 784 residents were “very grateful” for the Trump Organization’s investment there after it bought the site in 2014, insisting that his family were “welcome” there.
The U.S. president is joined in the remote corner of Ireland by his two sons, Eric and Don Jr, who have managed the family business since their 80-year-old father returned to the White House last year.
The former real estate magnate, who promotes its enterprises at every opportunity, told Martin that Doonbeg was “one of the greatest courses in the world.” The golf-mad president plays the game most weekends at one of his family’s U.S. properties.
He is even scheduled to host December’s G20 summit at his Miami golf resort.
Opposition Democrats in the US have long complained that blurring the lines between his presidency and personal business interests is corrupt, while some have called for an investigation into insider trading and market manipulation claims.
The White House has aggressively pushed back against claims of conflicts of interest and that Trump has been using his presidency to enrich himself.

Mild-mannered Canada shows the world how to take the fight to Trump
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:30:08 UTC
17:30:08 KST

Zhou Xiaoming is a senior fellow at the Centre for China and Globalisation in Beijing and a former deputy representative of China’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations Office in Geneva.
For anyone who has spent time living in Canada, the country’s default posture towards its southern neighbour has long felt almost hard-coded: polite, deferential, almost allergic to confrontation.
I saw this first-hand as a visiting scholar in the country in the early 1980s, when I met locals who embodied the national stereotype of moderation in all things. Canadians preferred compromise even when they had a right to push back, treating their far larger ally as a partner to be accommodated, not challenged.
This was not weakness but a deliberate choice rooted in geography, history and a belief that good relations with the United States were essential to Canadian prosperity. This is why Canada’s recent decision to walk away from talks and impose counter-tariffs on American goods landed like a thunderclap.
On August 22, after the US applied 50 per cent tariffs on US$20 billion worth of Canadian goods, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced that Canada would impose matching tariffs on American exports of the same scale.
Canada sends nearly three-quarters of its merchandise exports to the United States, it shares a border of nearly 9,000 kilometres with it and it is deeply integrated with its military and security apparatus through the North American Aerospace Defence Command. Its choice to stand up to the US is more than a news story – it is a turning point.
This rebellion of the reasonable carries three profound implications for the global order. For one, Canada’s stance should shatter any lingering illusions among US allies. The Trump administration’s treatment of Canada – including openly suggesting Canada should become the 51st state and reportedly demanding rollbacks of French-language and Quebec cultural protections – shows its nationalist world view respects no friendship, however old or intimate.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Sunday that US and Israeli attacks on Iran demonstrated that economic resilience cannot be sustained without security, warning that strikes on economic and energy infrastructure can have consequences beyond national borders.
Addressing the 18th BRICS Plus Summit, Pezeshkian said the effects of targeting a country’s economic, energy, and development infrastructure can rapidly spill across its borders and have regional and global repercussions.
He said Iranians, including women, children, and other civilians, had paid a heavy price for the attacks, while infrastructure built over decades for the country’s development had been damaged.

On economic cooperation, the Iranian president called for expanding trade in national currencies and strengthening the New Development Bank to increase BRICS members’ resilience against political and economic pressure.
He also said BRICS represents growing demand for a more balanced and inclusive global order in which no center of power has the right to “determine the fate of others.”
The remarks came on the final day of the two-day 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit in New Delhi, where leaders of the bloc and partner countries met for a session on resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability.
The expanded 11-member BRICS grouping includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.
On Saturday, the bloc adopted the New Delhi Declaration, pledging to deepen cooperation with emerging markets, developing countries, and BRICS partner nations.

Russian Strikes Hit Near Polish Border, Kyiv-Warsaw Train

2026-09-13
08:28:00 UTC
17:28:00 KST

Russian forces launched strikes near the Yahodyn-Dorohusk border crossing along Ukraine’s western border with Poland on Sunday morning, Sept. 13, damaging a filling station and hitting the locomotive of a passenger train en route to Warsaw.
The bombardment struck within two kilometers of the Polish border in the Volyn region, sparking a sharp diplomatic warning from Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, who described the cross-border escalation as Russian terror “knocking directly at the doors of the EU and NATO.”

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
According to Volyn Customs spokeswoman Valentyna Chernysh, falling munitions ignited a blaze at a commercial gas station complex and engulfed several parked freight trucks nearby.
State Border Guard Service (DPSU) spokesman Andriy Demchenko confirmed that incoming fire did not directly hit the border inspection infrastructure itself, though operations at the Yahodyn crossing were temporarily halted during the air raid alert while personnel and travelers sheltered.
The crossing subsequently resumed normal processing operations once the immediate threat subsided.
Concurrently, state rail operator Ukrzaliznytsia reported that Russian munitions struck the locomotive of a passenger train traveling from Kyiv to Warsaw approximately two kilometers from the Polish border.
Rail monitoring teams detected the incoming threat and issued an advance warning to the crew, averting casualties among passengers and rail staff.
Russian Strikes Injure 12 Across Odesa, Ternopil, and Konotop
Sybiha demands full Western embargo
Sybiha condemned the morning strikes, warning that Moscow is deliberately testing the boundaries of allied airspace and border security.
“Barbaric Russian strikes near the Ukrainian-Polish border in Yahodyn are not simply a continuation of attacks on Ukraine’s state borders. This is Putin’s terror knocking directly at the door of the EU and NATO. The Russian barbarians are already at your gates, dear partners,” Sybiha stated.
Sybiha appealed directly to Western allies to impose sweeping, non-incremental economic penalties to hold the Kremlin accountable.
“Act now: bring the full power of your sanctions against Putin’s aggressive regime,” Sybiha urged. “Make Moscow feel the consequences of its terror. Not partial decisions, but decisive and powerful steps: a full trade embargo, a total entry ban, and complete sanctions against the military-industrial complex.”
Persistent targeting of transport and fuel infrastructure
The border assault marks a further geographic expansion in Russia’s sustained aerial campaign targeting Ukraine’s transportation corridors and energy distribution networks.
On Saturday, Sept. 12, Russian strikes hit railway infrastructure in Fastiv, Kyiv region, and the western regional center of Lutsk, prompting Ukrzaliznytsia to evacuate passengers and railway staff.
The operator also truncated direct rail service to the northeastern city of Sumy, rerouting passenger journeys to Konotop and substituting bus transfers due to recurring attacks on rolling stock.
Earlier in the week, Russian strikes targeted four passenger trains across the Sumy, Zaporizhzhia, and Kharkiv regions over a 48-hour span, killing three people and injuring 20 others.
The damage to the filling station near Yahodyn also coincides with an escalating campaign against retail fuel networks across Ukraine.
On Saturday, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced that the government is testing automated early warning software to alert gas stations to incoming drone flight paths following deadly strikes on multiple fuel complexes in Kyiv that killed two people and injured four on Friday.

'This is the test': All eyes on US Fed to tackle high inflation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:27:50 UTC
17:27:50 KST

AFP Photo
The U.S. Federal Reserve goes into a key rate-setting meeting this week with markets expecting policymakers to pull the trigger on a rate hike to tackle persistently high inflation — and analysts say central bank chief Kevin Warsh's credibility is on the line.
The world's largest economy has been dealing with years of higher-than-target inflation, and prices have surged in the wake of US President Donald Trump's war on Iran, his signature tariff policies and the ongoing AI boom.
The Fed has held rates steady since January, choosing to wait to gauge the effects of energy price shocks and to let the tariffs' effects on prices ripple through the economy.
In recent weeks, however, several Fed policymakers — including Warsh himself — have hinted that if inflation does not show clear signs of slowing, the central bank will have to act by raising interest rates.
On Sept. 11, new data on consumer inflation for August showed it remaining steady at 3.4 percent — no change from the month before, but still well above the Fed's long-term 2 percent target.
Market expectations of a 25-basis-point rate hike on Sept. 16 surged in the wake of the data, with the probability at more than 85 percent according to CME's FedWatch tool.
The Fed last raised rates three years ago, when it was fighting surging inflation in the wake of the pandemic. They currently stand at between 3.5 and 3.75 percent.
Trump has railed against the Fed over interest rates since taking office for his second term, launching unprecedented attacks on the central bank's independence as he demands lower rates to spur economic activity.Warsh was appointed by Trump and analysts say this is his first real test since taking office: Will the Fed raise rates to combat inflation, or hold steady in line with what the White House prefers?
"This is the test. This is what comes with that job, and now he has to decide how to handle it," said David Wessel, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution.
"He's either going to completely disappoint the markets, or he runs the risk that he's going to start to anger Donald Trump."
"It's quite likely that the Fed will raise interest rates next week," said Claudia Sahm, chief economist at investment firm New Century Advisors who previously worked at the Fed.
But "it's not a done deal," she cautioned in comments to AFP. "This is a difficult decision for them to make."
Sahm warned such a move was "not a magic wand and it is a costly medicine."
She said the Fed could still hold rates steady rather than administer that medicine, but it would have to explain its decision clearly to markets.
"If they surprise markets and they can't explain why they're surprising markets, then Wednesday afternoon will be pretty messy," she said.
Since taking office, Warsh has changed the way the Fed communicates about its decisions, advocating for less transparency into the process as he thinks it locks policymakers into courses of action that may need to be adjusted.
Investors have had mixed reactions to the cut in what is known as "forward guidance," with analysts saying it has introduced more uncertainty into how financial markets price in inflation and interest rate expectations.
Warsh has advocated in the past for lower interest rates due to expected productivity gains from AI technology, but in recent weeks he has doubled down on the Fed's mandate to bring inflation down.
"There's always been this doubt about whether Kevin Warsh is going to be like his predecessors and do what's right for the economy, even if it's politically inconvenient," said Wessel of Brookings.
"If he raises rates now and Trump goes ballistic, he will have established his credibility as an independent Fed chair for the rest of his term.

The 2026/27 heating season: when Ukrainians can expect heat in their homes
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
11:26:26 EEST
17:26:26 KST

The 2026/27 heating season: when Ukrainians can expect heat in their homes
Kyiv • UNN
Heating will start after three days with an average temperature of up to +8 °C, by decision of the local authorities. Communities are 79.2% ready.
With the first nighttime cold spells and frosts, despite the fact that it is still only the beginning of September on the calendar, Ukrainians have many questions about the new heating season. People want to know when to expect heat in a particular city, who decides when heat supply to buildings begins, and whether the condition of the networks will allow hot water to be supplied to radiators.
When Ukrainian homes will be warm and what needs to be known about the new heating season was выяснено by UNN.
What determines the start of heat supply to buildings
It is worth recalling that in Ukraine there is no single day when heating is switched on simultaneously in all cities. The start of the heating season is tied primarily to the temperature, while the final decision is made by local authorities.
Under the current rules approved by Resolution No. 830 of the Cabinet of Ministers, the decision to begin the heating period is made by local self-government bodies, taking into account the weather and the requirements of technical and sanitary standards. Under these standards, the heating period must begin no later than when the average daily temperature does not exceed +8 °C for three consecutive days. It is important to emphasize that this refers specifically to the average daily temperature, not the thermometer reading in the morning or at night.
The +8 °C standard for three consecutive days also does not mean that heating will automatically be switched on in all regions of Ukraine on the fourth day. In different regions, temperatures fall to this level at different times, and heating networks are in different condition. Some social infrastructure facilities, including hospitals, kindergartens, and schools, may be connected separately based on decisions by communities and requests from institution heads.
How decisions on the start of the heating season are made in cities
The mechanism is decentralized: the city, town, or village authorities determine when the heating period begins in their community, after which heat-supply companies start the equipment and connect consumers. After that, heat does not necessarily appear simultaneously in all buildings in the city. The heat-transfer medium is supplied in stages, while the actual time when heat reaches a particular apartment depends on the operation of the boiler house, the condition of the networks, and the building’s internal system.
Communities began preparing for the 2026/27 heating season in advance. According to Cabinet of Ministers data, as of September 7, the readiness of Ukraine’s housing stock to receive the heat-transfer medium stood at 79.2%. This means that more than 114,000 of the nearly 144,000 planned buildings had already been prepared for winter.
Damage to energy infrastructure caused by Russian attacks remains a separate factor. Thus, Naftogaz has already reported that since the beginning of 2026, Russian forces have carried out 287 attacks on facilities belonging to its group. Therefore, this season, the start of heating depends primarily on a particular community’s ability to maintain heat supply in the event of accidents or power outages.
What to do if your home is cold after heat is supplied
If the heating season has already been declared in the community, but the radiators in an apartment remain cold, the first step is to contact the service provider or building manager and document the problem. The address, the time during which heat was absent, and the temperature in the room should be reported. For residential premises in buildings whose design documentation was approved before October 1, 2005, the standard temperature is +18 °C. For newer housing stock, the relevant state building standards apply.
If the heat-supply service is provided improperly or heat is not supplied to the building at all, the law gives consumers the right to demand an inspection and the preparation of a statement of claim. The State Service of Ukraine on Food Safety and Consumer Protection explains to Ukrainians that a representative of the service provider or building manager must arrive within the period specified in the contract, but no later than one day after the request. Following the inspection, the representative draws up a statement. If the preparation of the statement is refused, or if a representative of the management company fails to arrive at all, residents may prepare the document themselves, with the signatures of the consumer and other residents.
If a confirmed violation is established, the consumer may demand a recalculation of the service charge. At the same time, it is worth remembering that the cause of the low temperature may lie not only in the work of the heat supplier. The thermometer reading in a room is affected by the condition of the building’s internal system, windows, building insulation, and so on.
When to expect heat in apartments in 2026
As of September 11, it is impossible to name an exact nationwide start date for the 2026/27 season. The decisive factors remain the actual temperature conditions in autumn and the security situation in the country, which affects the technical ability to supply heat to apartments.
The Ukrainian Hydrometeorological Center forecast an average monthly temperature of 11–18 °C for September, which is close to the climatic norm. Therefore, there are currently no grounds to expect the mass start of heating in September. Consequently, October traditionally remains the reference point for consumers.
However, heating may be needed earlier in the northern, western, and mountainous areas of the country, while in the southern regions the season may shift to a later date. Therefore, Ukrainians should focus more on the actual temperature and announcements by local authorities than on October 15, a date that people have traditionally regarded as the unconditional start of the heating season.
Reminder
At the end of August 2026, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy put into effect a decision of the National Security and Defense Council on the status of implementation of the Comprehensive Plans for Regional Resilience and preparations for the 2026/2027 heating season. The National Security and Defense Council obliged the regions to strengthen infrastructure protection, increase backup power supplies by 20%, and create a two-week fuel reserve.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Former NBA star Dwight Howard returned to Taiwan on Sunday to headline the Kings Heart Classic charity event at Xinzhuang Gymnasium in New Taipei.
The 40-year-old Howard, an eight-time NBA All-Star and eight-time All-NBA selection, was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame as part of its 2025 class. He also won three consecutive NBA Defensive Player of the Year awards from 2009 to 2011, per UDN.
Howard previously played professionally in Taiwan for the Taoyuan Leopards during the 2022-23 T1 League season. He led the league in rebounding, was selected to the All-Defensive First Team and All-T1 League First Team, and was named the league’s Most Valuable Import.
Sunday's event, organized by the New Taipei Kings and The Asian Tournament, featured a friendly game between the Kings and the Macau Black Knights before Howard’s charity exhibition game. Howard served as a guest commentator for the first game and was set to lead the TAT All-Star team against a Kings All-Star team in the charity game. A fan meet-and-greet was also scheduled between the two games, per a Kings press release.
Part of the event’s proceeds will be donated to PACK Taiwan, an animal welfare organization, to improve shelter care and support the adoption of stray dogs, according to the Kings.
After arriving at his hotel at about 1 a.m., Howard said he still had enough time to enjoy one of his favorite Taiwanese delicacies, chicken butts. He also described Taiwan as one of his favorite places in the world and hinted at the possibility of playing professionally in Taiwan again, per UDN.
When asked about returning to play in Taiwan, Howard gave a long “hmm” before laughing. He said his children are now grown up and that he wants to spend more time with his family. Returning to Taiwan after about three years, Howard said memories of his previous time in the country came flooding back and that he was already moved to tears when he arrived at his hotel.
Howard recently announced that he will return to professional basketball with Black Fortress Tbilisi in Georgia. He is expected to join the club in October after announcing his retirement earlier this year, per BasketNews.
Howard said he loves the enthusiasm and friendliness of Taiwanese people and that many of his friends in Taiwan are like family. He joked that numerous players have messaged him asking about Taiwan and encouraged them to visit the country and create their own memories.

Taiwan Fisheries Agency defends new Kaohsiung crew quarters
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:25:46 UTC
17:25:46 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Fisheries Agency defended the newly built Cianjhen fishing port crew quarters in Kaohsiung, saying the facility is intended to improve living conditions for fishers returning to port.
The agency rejected recent news reports describing the facility as a “luxury bathhouse” and said there is no ongoing water shortage. The building opened on June 10, 2025, and provides multiple services, including accommodation, showers, prayer rooms, internet access, and rest areas, it said in a press release.
On July 1, a temporary water outage occurred due to a break in an external water pipeline, but repairs were completed the same day, and there is currently no water shortage, the agency said. During peak periods for squid fishing vessels in June and July, thousands of crew members may return to the port within a short time, leading to high demand for showers and other water facilities. Occasional spikes in water demand may occur, but there is no full-scale water outage, the agency said.
The agency said it has coordinated with fishermen’s associations and related organizations to encourage crew members to stagger usage and better manage peak and off-peak water demand.
The agency acknowledged that a small number of guest rooms have occasionally had odors. It said measures including improved ventilation, replacement of odor-resistant floor drains, and testing of heat-recovery ventilators have been carried out, while contractors continue to investigate isolated cases.
The agency said foreign crew members who have used the facility have expressed appreciation for its showers, rest areas, prayer rooms, internet access, and accommodation, indicating that the facility helps improve living conditions for crews returning to port.

Dialogue about Fakes 4.0 forum to strengthen fact-checking cooperation — GFCN chief

MOSCOW, September 13. /TASS/. The international Dialogue about Fakes forum, scheduled for September 22 in Moscow, will help participants consolidate agreements on fact-checking, Vladimir Tabak, president of the Global Fact-Checking Network (GFCN), told TASS ahead of the event.
He said the forum’s community grows larger and stronger each year, while talks with several countries are advancing. "International projects are reaching a new level, as are negotiations with a number of countries. For me, this is an opportunity to consolidate agreements, in both formal and informal settings, and make a concerted effort to draw attention once again to the field in which our partners and I have been working for several years," Tabak said.
The GFCN chief also thanked the Foreign Ministry for its longstanding support and said Russia’s top diplomat Sergey Lavrov would attend this year’s forum in person. "We certainly could not have organized an event on this scale without the Foreign Ministry. This year, Sergey Lavrov will take part in person. We are very grateful to him for responding to our requests. We are also grateful to [Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman] Maria Zakharova for her unwavering support," he added.
Tabak stressed that the forum continues to grow each year. "We will have more participants than last year, so yes, the event will be larger. But it is not about the number of participants. We focus primarily on the level of representation and the standing of the experts taking part. That, too, is higher than in previous years, which is a significant achievement for us," he concluded.
GFCN
The Global Fact-Checking Network brings together experts and fact-checking organizations worldwide. The association was founded by the TASS news agency, the nonprofit organization Dialogue Regions and the New Media Workshop to combat disinformation. More than 125 journalists from 55 countries already collaborate with GFCN on fact-checking.
The international Dialogue about Fakes 4.0 forum will take place on September 22 at the Russia National Center in Moscow. TASS is the event’s strategic partner.

1,200 designers submitted visuals for new euro banknotes
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

1,200 designers submitted visuals for new euro banknotes
With new security features now available, the European Central Bank wanted to redesign euro banknotes, says designer Anne Pikkov. She represented Estonia on the jury that carried out the pre‑selection for the new euro banknote designs.
"Euro banknotes have been in our wallets for more than 20 years. During that time, new security measures have been invented, paper and inks have improved, and values have changed. When the first series was created, Europe was united through architectural styles and heritage. The ECB wanted to review whether these visuals still speak to Europeans today, or whether new unifying elements are needed," Pikkov said.
The ECB set certain criteria. "Two themes were selected: 'European Culture' and 'Birds and Rivers'. Otherwise, designers had free hands. A total of 1,200 designers across Europe submitted proposals."
The jury included not only designers but also psychologists and neuroscientists. "We discussed the size of numerals, color intensity, and how the people depicted should represent specific fields," Pikkov said. "If the previous banknotes showed objects, the new ones will show the European person — their skills and achievements."
The public will also have a say. "Right now the vote is in people's hands. Anyone interested can indicate which directions they prefer. Based on this, the ECB will shape its final decision," she noted.
Five Estonian designers took part in the competition, though none reached the final selection.
For birds, the criterion was that they must be European species that migrate between European countries. "For rivers, designers could depict rapids, puddles, rain — even water crystals."
Although cash use may seem rare in Estonia, half of all transactions in Europe are still made with banknotes. "Digital payments didn't replace anything — they simply added another option," Pikkov said.
Existing banknotes will remain in circulation; the new designs will be added alongside them.
The new visuals can be viewed on European Central Bank 's website.

UN warns Ukraine could face toughest winter since start of full-scale war

UN warns Ukraine could face toughest winter since start of full-scale war
Alexander De Croo, head of the UN development agency, said this in an interview with the BBC, Ukrinform reports.
According to him, Ukraine is entering the winter period "from a very weak base" due to Russia's "very systematic" targeting of civilian and energy infrastructure.
"This is petrol stations, it's shopping malls, it's business centers, but it's especially energy infrastructure, energy transmission lines, and so on. There is absolutely no justification for that," the UN official said.
He stressed that the UN is " very, very worried... about what this winter could become."
De Croo warned that extensive damage to energy and critical infrastructure could lead to disruptions in heating, water supply and sewage systems.
"With the temperatures that you would get here [winter temperatures in Ukraine can drop to -20C] that would lead to circumstances which would be really close to humanitarian catastrophe. […] This winter is going to be the toughest one since the war," the UN official said.
He said there was now a "race against the clock" to repair the power network before winter sets in and temperatures plummet. UNDP is helping Ukraine restore damaged infrastructure and develop more resilient and decentralized energy facilities that are less vulnerable to Russian attacks.
De Croo described restoring the energy system amid constant attacks as "almost an impossible task." He stressed that workers are forced to repair facilities during air raid alerts, and they know they are working at a site that is a target, while the threat of strikes means some work has to be suspended.
Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said earlier that Ukraine was significantly better prepared for Russian attacks this winter than it was a year ago.

A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:16:00 UTC
17:16:00 KST

A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
September 13, 2026
The painting on the canvas is of a man playing chess with a robot. The color on his face is still damp and glistening. Norbert Olah was working into the early hours: The Bura Galeria in Budapest has been his studio all summer. He finds it easiest to concentrate at night, when the Hungarian capital gradually falls silent.
Olah has taped foil and cardboard over the tiled floor at the back of the gallery. Pots of brushes, tubes of paint, pencil sketches, and, over and over again, pictures that include the blue-and-green Roma flag line the room.
Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he deliberately left this part of his identity out of his art. Not because his ethnicity wasn't important to him, but because he didn't want to be labeled a "Romani artist."
"There are so many prejudices about Roma culture and Roma art," Olah says. "The art scene regards it as naïve, unprofessional, unsophisticated, and kitsch."
But the older Olah got, the harder he found it to ignore his own story in his art. Especially in a country in which being Romani is not just an ethnicity but a political reality.
Life under Orban
The first time Viktor Orban's Fidesz party won an absolute majority in the Hungarian parliamentary elections of 2010, Olah had just finished school and was starting his art course at the Hungarian University of Fine Arts in Budapest. At a time of life when the world ought to be opening up, Olah felt more and more barriers were being erected.
Olah was directly affected by Hungary's political reorientation, as both an artist and a Romani. Politics co-opted the cultural scene and made it toe the party line. Roma became the target of hateful rhetoric, including from the prime minister himself. Orban repeatedly called attention to himself with racist comments about Roma.
For the 16 years Orban was in power, Hungary's Roma population, estimated to be around 700,000 people, was caught between official promises of integration and persistent marginalization. Orban's government introduced a state employment program that hired predominantly Romani workers. But instead of helping them gain a foothold in the job market, many Romani found themselves trapped in insecure, poorly paid, temporary jobs. The government did little to implement real change. Romani in Hungary are still disproportionately affected by poverty and social exclusion.
There came a point when Norbert Olah felt he could no longer stand by and do nothing.
Other people's prejudices
In 2021, during Hungary's biggest independent contemporary art event, the OFF-Biennale Budapest, Olah and his father laid a brick wall directly in front of the entrance to the building that had housed the Roma Parliament, a Roma cultural center with an art collection, archive, library, and events program. The Orban government evicted it in 2016, saying the building was structurally dangerous and promising to repurpose it as a national Roma center. It has stood empty ever since.
The title of Olah's work was "The Romani Artist's Fears." Words like "integration," "assimilation," and "segregation" were chiseled into the bricks. A few weeks later, Olah staged a performance in which he took a sledgehammer to his artwork and smashed it till it collapsed.
In an accompanying text, Olah wrote publicly for the first time about the fears, prejudices, and expectations he encounters as an artist with Roma roots. The text is full of questions. Should a Romani artist's work focus on topics relevant to Roma? What is the relationship between ethnicity and aesthetics? Would people only contact an artist with Roma roots if they were specifically looking for a Romani artist, or would they do so if they needed a Hungarian artist, too?
"Of course we're always looking for answers. But sometimes it's more interesting to look at the question itself," says Olah, picking a piece of crepe masking tape off the floor. "If it feels uncomfortable, it's a good question."
And so Olah has created a new label for Romani artists. The Bura Galeria, established by Romani activists in 2021 in Budapest's District 8, has become the place for it: A platform for contemporary Roma art.
"We're not asking to be accepted by the art scene," said Olah. "We're opening the door and inviting others in."
Open antiziganism
Identity and exclusion, power and the misuse of power — these became central themes for Olah's artistic work. He had no lack of inspiration during the Orban years.
Although Fidesz's policies were hardly favorable to Roma, Orban's party could, for a long time, count on Roma votes — for example, because local employment programs enabled local politicians to pressure socially underprivileged voters. There were also many documented cases of vote-buying. Fidesz was so confident that the majority of Roma would continue to vote for it that it openly fueled the antiziganism still widespread in Hungarian society.
Shortly before the election in April 2026, Fidesz's Janos Lazar, who was minister for transport at the time, spoke out against labor migration with the argument that Hungary still had "domestic reserves," like the Roma, who could "clean the crap out of overflowing toilets" on Intercity trains. The scene appears in Olah's art: A fake election poster depicts a man in a balaclava sitting on a golden toilet, brandishing a toilet brush, with the slogan underneath: "Gypsy Criminals for President."
Opportunity for real change?
Gypsy Criminals is also the name of the artists' collective Olah founded in 2024, along with a friend of his and his miniature pinscher. The term comes from Hungarian crime statistics, and has been used since the 2000s by right-wing politicians to imply that all Roma are criminals. The name is ironic, like many aspects of Olah's work.
Analyses by the foundation Roma for Democracy show that many Roma did not vote for Orban's Fidesz party in the April 2026 parliamentary election. Orban's successor, Peter Magyar, adopted a different tone in relation to Roma as part of his election campaign. He met with members of the Roma minority, and his election manifesto contained a specific paragraph about equal opportunities for Roma. Four of the Tisza party's nine new members of parliament are Romani. One was even elected a deputy speaker of parliament.
Since the election, there has been cautious optimism that the precarious situation of many Roma in Hungary could finally change. On the other hand, nothing has fundamentally changed in the four months since the election, apart from the tone when talking about the ethnic minority. "What I'm seeing right now are mostly symbolic gestures," says Olah.
Roma on Mars
Some of his friends in the more liberal art scene are growing impatient. They would like to see Magyar take a much more liberal course, but Olah is a realist.
"He's a conservative politician," he says. "We elected him to put an end to the Orban system. He didn't promise any more than that." But the election in April was an opportunity for a fresh political start, he adds. "I think in the long run we will live in a normal society again, led by a normal government, that will do some things well and others not so well. As an artist, it will be my job to criticize that."
Olah's work also considers the future. The first pictures for his next project are already up on the wall in his studio. It's Roma futurism: A Romani couple strolling on Mars; a blue-and-green Roma flag on the moon; a weightless astronaut with a traditional Cegled water jug, used by Romani musicians as a percussion instrument. Olah is also planning a two-meter-high space station in the shape of a cartwheel, a symbol of the Romani people.
For Olah, space travel is also a metaphor for social advancement — the desire of people and communities to overcome the barriers they face as a result of their origins, or poverty, or life in a minority. Again, he is asking questions. What if a society were fundamentally recreated from the beginning? If aliens encountered Roma, would they do so without prejudice? What remains of an identity if everything about it changes?
Olah shreds the masking tape between his fingers. More unanswered questions. But that's exactly what makes them so interesting.

Ramzi Mahmoud and Sahin Demir
13 September 2026•Update: 13 September 2026
Two Palestinians were killed and 13 others injured in an Israeli drone strike targeting a vehicle in southern Gaza City on Sunday, a medical source told Anadolu.
The source said an Israeli drone struck a civilian vehicle in the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood, killing two Palestinians and leaving 13 others with various injuries.
Witnesses told Anadolu that the drone fired at least two missiles at the vehicle, killing its two occupants immediately and injuring nearby passersby.
Separately, Israeli forces fired artillery shells toward Palestinian homes northeast of the Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza, according to local sources.
Israeli military vehicles also opened heavy fire toward buildings and tents housing displaced Palestinians in southern Khan Younis, while Israeli warships fired toward the city’s coastline, witnesses said.
Israeli violations of the ceasefire agreement, in effect since Oct. 10, 2025, have killed 1,369 Palestinians and injured 4,627 others as of Saturday, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.
Israel’s war on Gaza since October 2023 has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians and injured over 174,000, while causing widespread destruction across the enclave, according to Gaza authorities.

Fire breaks out on vessel after projectile strike in Strait of Hormuz: UKMTO
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:13:00 UTC
17:13:00 KST

Sahin Demir
13 September 2026•Update: 13 September 2026
A fire broke out aboard a vessel after it was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said Sunday.
UKMTO said it received the initial report of the incident at 2300GMT on Saturday, without specifying the exact time the vessel was struck.
The maritime authority initially said the status of the crew, the extent of damage to the vessel and any environmental impact were unknown.
In an update issued Sunday, UKMTO said a fire had broken out aboard the vessel following the reported attack.
Local authorities were at the scene and assisting in evacuating crew members, it added.
UKMTO advised vessels transiting the area to exercise caution and report any suspicious activity as authorities investigate the incident.
The incident comes amid a series of attacks on commercial shipping linked to the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Several merchant vessels have recently been targeted in the northern Gulf, Gulf of Oman, and waters off Iraq.
Separately, Iranian authorities said Sunday that one person was killed and three others were injured when a commercial vessel was struck near Hengam Island, off southern Iran’s Qeshm Island, in what Iranian state media described as a US attack.

Russians attack Ukraine's second-largest pharmaceutical warehouse twice

Russians attack Ukraine's second-largest pharmaceutical warehouse twice
Russian forces have attacked one of Ukraine's largest pharmaceutical warehouses, Universal Logistic, for two days in a row.
Source: a source in the pharmaceutical market
Details: Universal Logistic is one of Ukraine's two largest pharmaceutical warehouses. The other, Biocon, was attacked by Russian forces on 3 September.
The Universal Logistic warehouse is located in the Boryspil district in Kyiv Oblast. It met the highest standards for pharmaceutical storage. According to the company's website, the total area of its warehouse facilities is 21,000 sq m.
The warehouse serves the country's largest pharmaceutical distributors, which then deliver medicines to pharmacies. Due to the attacks on the warehouse and constant air-raid warnings, suppliers have been unable to remove goods from the Universal Logistic facility.
Ukrainska Pravda has no information on any casualties resulting from the attack.
On the evening of 12 September, Kyiv Oblast Military Administration reported that Russian forces had damaged warehouse facilities in the Boryspil district.
Background:
- Some regions of Ukraine have seen increased demand for certain medicines, causing stocks in pharmacies to decline, and in some cases the available supplies may last for only two to three weeks.
- Meanwhile, on 10 September, Edem Adamanov, Head of the State Expert Centre of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine, said that Russian attacks on pharmaceutical warehouses have not caused a shortage of medicines in Ukraine, and that pharmacy chains have supplies for one to two months.

Australia reports first bird flu case in endangered sea lion
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
16:11:19 CST
17:11:19 KST

CANBERRA, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Australian authorities on Sunday reported the first case of the H5N1 avian influenza in an endangered sea lion.
Environment Minister in South Australia (SA), Emily Bourke, told reporters that testing detected the highly pathogenic strain in an Australian sea lion that was found dead on Friday on Kangaroo Island about 100 km off the coast of Adelaide.
She said that the sea lion was already being monitored while it recovered from a shark attack.
"We found that it was actually not the shark attack that killed the sea lion. It was the bird flu," Bourke said.
The National Parks and Wildlife Service estimates that there are fewer than 12,000 Australian sea lions in the wild, 85 percent of which are in SA.
Kangaroo Island's Seal Bay, where the bird flu case was detected, is home to the third largest colony of Australian sea lions.
"We've seen quite a number of mammal cases, but the Australian sea lion is the rarest seal found in our Australian waters," Bourke said.
According to the latest national data, as of Friday, there had been 521 confirmed events of H5N1 bird flu in Australia, 286 of which have been in SA. ■

ZAGREB, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- A large wildfire burning on the Croatian island of Brac for days has spread toward villages and tourist facilities overnight, prompting the evacuation of more than 200 people, local media reported Sunday.
Fanned by strong winds, the fire advanced toward the town of Milna, prompting authorities to activate an early warning system for residents. More than 200 people were evacuated as a precaution.
Chief Firefighting Commander Slavko Tucakovic told local media that no one had suffered serious injuries, although some people had inhaled smoke. No serious health consequences had been reported so far.
Croatia has been hit by a string of major wildfires this summer amid unusually hot and dry weather. A massive fire that broke out near the coastal town of Omis in southern Croatia in August claimed three lives in one of the deadliest wildfire incidents the country has seen in recent years. ■

Scenic spots, schools closed in south China as tropical depression brings heavy rain
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
16:10:46 CST
17:10:46 KST

HAIKOU, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Authorities in China's southern island province of Hainan have suspended classes in parts of the province and closed 27 tourist attractions as a tropical depression over the South China Sea unleashes torrential rain across the region.
Heavy rainfall is expected to persist over the next three days. Primary and secondary schools, kindergartens, and off-campus training institutions in parts of Hainan, including Wanning City, are to suspend classes for one to two days starting Sunday, depending on local conditions.
The Hainan Meteorological Service upgraded its rainstorm warning from Level III to Level II at 10:30 a.m. on Sunday. At 11 a.m., the provincial committee for disaster prevention, mitigation and relief elevated its flood and wind emergency response to Level II.
As of 11 a.m. on Sunday, the tropical depression was located in waters about 245 km west-southwest of the city of Sanya in Hainan, with maximum winds of 12 meters per second near its center. The system is expected to make landfall along the central coast of Vietnam on Sunday afternoon or evening.
The Ministry of Water Resources and the China Meteorological Administration (CMA) on Saturday jointly issued a blue alert for flash floods in parts of southeastern Hainan. Also on Saturday, the Ministry of Natural Resources and the CMA jointly issued a yellow alert for geological disaster risks in some areas of southeastern Hainan.
China has a four-tier emergency response system, with Level I being the most severe level. It also has a four-tier, color-coded weather warning system, with red representing the most severe warning, followed by orange, yellow and blue. ■

Türkiye, Azerbaijan seek deeper cooperation, says energy minister
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:09:09 UTC
17:09:09 KST

DHA Photo
Türkiye and Azerbaijan are advancing major electricity projects, Turkish Energy and Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar has stated, highlighting plans to expand regional energy connectivity while supporting Europe’s energy security.
Speaking after attending the 5th Türkiye-Azerbaijan Energy Forum in Baku last week, Bayraktar said the world has become a place of recurring crises and that crises are now the “new normal.” He said Türkiye and Azerbaijan are responding by developing more predictable, diversified and deeper cooperation in the energy sector.
Bayraktar recalled landmark projects including the Baku-Tbilisi-Erzurum Natural Gas Pipeline, the Trans-Anatolian Natural Gas Pipeline (TANAP) and the Trans Adriatic Pipeline (TAP).
“TANAP has delivered 100 billion cubic meters of natural gas as of this year,” he said, adding that the pipeline makes a significant contribution to Europe’s energy supply security.
The minister said existing projects such as the Baku-Tbilisi-Erzurum pipeline, the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan (BTC) oil pipeline and TANAP should be utilized at full capacity.
According to Bayraktar, around 600,000 barrels of oil currently flow through the BTC pipeline, while its capacity stands at 1 million barrels per day.
He said the route should also be used to transport crude oil from Central Asia and other parts of the Turkic world, adding that similar efforts could be undertaken in the natural gas sector.
Bayraktar said major electricity projects are currently under discussion.
“We are discussing three main projects,” he said. “These include a power transmission line from Nakhchivan to Türkiye, the four-party green energy corridor connecting Türkiye, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Bulgaria, and another electricity transmission line that will reach Europe via the Black Sea.”
He said the projects would further strengthen regional energy cooperation and connectivity across the wider region.

Budanov Eyes Trilateral Ukraine Peace Talks in October
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:09:00 UTC
17:09:00 KST

Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine Kyrylo Budanov announced that a renewed round of peace negotiations in a trilateral format could take place in early October, focusing on de-escalating aerial strikes and securing Black Sea maritime shipping.
Speaking on the sidelines of the annual Yalta European Strategy (YES 2026) forum in Kyiv, Budanov stated that direct diplomatic engagement involving Ukraine, the US, and European allies is essential to establishing a workable framework to reduce combat intensity.

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“It is important that the United States and Europe take part in the negotiations,” Budanov emphasized, expressing confidence that the next negotiation track could convene next month.
According to Budanov, an initial agreement would center on practical, step-by-step de-escalation measures rather than an immediate comprehensive political settlement.
“The primary issue will be Black Sea maritime transit, reducing the volume of strikes against civilian objects, critical infrastructure, and similar priorities,” Budanov said. “Everyone exchanged views on this matter. The Russians are well aware of this and are also considering how to handle it. We are waiting.”
The presidential chief of staff added that Ukraine and its partners must accelerate efforts to construct a durable post-war European security architecture, reiterating that Ukraine and the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) must constitute an indispensable component of that defense framework, as President Volodymyr Zelensky has consistently advocated.
Ukraine Tests Automated Drone Warning System for Gas Stations
Consultations with European security advisers
Budanov’s remarks followed high-level diplomatic discussions on the sidelines of the YES forum with European national security advisers, including Germany’s Günter Sautter, France’s Emmanuel Bonne, Italy’s Fabrizio Saggio, and the United Kingdom’s Jonathan Powell.
Budanov also held an expanded bilateral meeting with the British delegation to align strategic positions and coordinate joint diplomatic responses ahead of multilateral autumn summits.
The diplomatic consultations in Kyiv follow a visit the previous weekend by European national security advisers and US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who traveled overland to Kyiv following talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
Upcoming New York diplomatic engagements
The prospect of October negotiations coincides with planned high-level diplomatic engagements scheduled for late September.
President Volodymyr Zelensky announced during a visit to Canada that he expects to meet US President Donald Trump in New York on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly to clarify the next stages of the diplomatic process.
“At the end of September, we will have an opportunity to meet, I think, with the American team in New York,” Zelensky said, indicating that direct talks with Trump would provide greater insight into Washington’s mediation efforts.
Zelensky noted that Ukrainian and American teams maintain constant dialogue regarding energy security and Black Sea export routes.
Diplomatic tracks have intensified following an hour-long phone conversation between Trump and Putin on Tuesday, Sept. 8.
According to Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov, the discussion focused on conflict resolution parameters in Ukraine, during which Putin presented battlefield assessments and outlined Moscow’s conditions for a cessation of hostilities.

To recap: In the past 48 hours, Reform UK has received a staggering sum of £72m from two crypto billionaires, the largest single donations in British political history.
Christopher Harborne’s £36m donation, which he announced in the Telegraph newspaper yesterday, matches that given by another cryptocurrency investor Ben Delo on Friday.
Rayner: 'Hundreds of people in black, with balaclavas, is intimidatory and crosses the line'
Rayner was also asked earlier on the BBC about the surge in anti-migrant protests, including those yesterday in Portsmouth, Tamworth and Glasgow where face coverings were banned.
Police brought in the restriction after the September 5-6 weekend where hundreds of masked, black-clad men blocked entry to the Port of Dover and obstructed roads in Portsmouth in menacing scenes.
“We’ve been really clear that there is a right to protest in this country, but it doesn’t give you a right to intimidate and act unlawfully… We’ve seen a surge of divisiveness and that has made communities feel more vulnerable and that is not acceptable,” Rayner said.
As warnings surrounding the threats of AI continue to make headlines this weekend my colleague Dan Milmo has written a less pessimistic piece on the topic in his feature from the AI bootcamps aimed at addressing UK youth unemployment.
The UK government is trying to address two of the greatest challenges facing the national economy: AI and youth unemployment and a pilot project in Preston comes with apprenticeship offer for Neets at end of three-week course.
George Osborne calls for UK to rejoin EU customs union and boost trade
Elsewhere today the former chancellor George Osborne said Britain’s economy had “fallen off a cliff” since Brexit and that rejoining the European Union’s customs union would be the fastest route to recovery.
Only slim chance target of building 1.5m homes in England will be met, minister says
While talking to the media this morning Angela Rayner also admitted that there was only a slim chance government will meet target of building 1.5m home.
Labour’s manifesto pledge to build 1.5m houses by the next election was a “stretch target”, the communities secretary added, but said it was not being ditched and she was “definitely not giving up”.
My colleague Jessica Elgot has her reported in detail here:
Angela Rayner said she was pleased AI companies are “talking about the threats as well as the opportunities” after Elon Musk and Sam Altman backed a call for the industry to slow down development, PA reports.
It comes after Anthropic boss Dario Amodei said he was concerned that since this summer, AI has been “advancing drastically faster”.
Given the rate of development, Mr Amodei is worried that within six to 12 months, AI could be capable of leading a swarm that could take over the entire internet.
The entrepreneur, whose company is behind the AI assistant Claude, shared a three-part plan for building the technology at a “balanced rate”.
Rayner told Sky News: “I’m pleased that these companies are also talking about the threats as well as the opportunities that AI presents to us, and we have to work with our international partners, which is what we’re doing.”
Describing the UK as “world leaders” in AI security, the communities and housing secretary added: “We have put robust systems in place here in the UK, like the AI Security Institute, to make sure we’re building resilience so that we get the benefit as well as really understand and protect against any risk.”
Conservative MP Tom Tugendhat told Sky News: “The speed of change is also extraordinary, and this is where actually government can enable a conversation, but we simply do not have the speed to keep up with the advances that are happening.
“And the reality is, we can’t pass laws against mathematics.
“These are mathematical equations that are being developed in greater and greater speed, and we need to maintain that ability to protect ourselves.”
£72m Reform injection equivalent to entire year of political donations
Let’s put this £72m weekend windfall for Reform in context – not only the largest single donations to a UK political party ever, but also the equivalent essentially of an entire year of political donations in the lead-up to a general election.
A total of £79m was donated to UK political parties in 2023, according to the Electoral Commission. A further £84m was given in 2024, the election year.
This is just what’s been publicly logged. Reform is also facing allegations it has tried to hide foreign donations. It denies any wrongdoing.
The data also shows how much has been donated to parties since the 2024 vote (not reflecting Reform’s latest endowments.)
Will also point out here that across the Sunday politics shows this morning, neither Labour nor the Tories ruled out accepting such huge sums from crypto-billionaires in the future.
Nigel Farage says that donations just go to putting Reform on a “more level playing field” with the more established parties.
Angela Rayner was asked on the BBC, at least three times, whether Labour on principle would have accepted tens of millions of pounds from the industry if they had been offered it.
She declined to give a direct answer, saying instead that the party has “very robust rules and a vetting process for where we accept donations from. And we have refused donations in the past.”
Tom Tugendhat meanwhile highlighted “problematic” areas of the crypto industry, but also didn’t answer the BBC’s question directly.
“Well, look, we’d accept money from reputable sources” he said, before turning to speculation on whether Reform had done their adequate checks.
Jenrick says there's 'economic opportunity' for UK from crypto
Reform has been describing these crypto billionaire donations – again the largest single gift to a British political party – as being from patriotic businessmen who “simply support our agenda”. Pressed by Laura Kuennsberg on the BBC: “And part of your agenda is being very pro cryptocurrency, which is their business?”
Jenrick replies, “Um, not really”, saying first that he wants “proper” regulation of the digital currency which is a bit of a “Wild West”, and then advancing to the idea of gains for the UK in adopting crypto.
Throughout this morning, he’s been referring to himself as Reform Shadow Chancellor.
“Is there an economic opportunity for the UK from crypto? Yes, and I want, as Reform Shadow Chancellor of UK, to seize that so we can compete with Dubai and the United States.”
“But that’s not what we’re doing here with these donations.”
Reform has said if it wins government, it would raise a law to boost adoption of crypto, including throuhg cutting tax on digital assets. They would also create a bitcoin reserve fund at the Bank of England.
Just wanted to highlight this statement too from Jenrick, insisting to both the BBC and Sky this morning that wealthy donors wouldn’t get formal favours, if Reform were to come into power.
He said “there are all these people in the House of Lords who are Tory donors. 24 out of the last 25 Tory Party treasurers sit in the House of Lords.”
“Reform is different. We are not going to give peerages, or knighthoods, to people who go around giving us donations,” he says.
A reminder that Jenrick was a Tory MP for 12 years (and the former shadow justice secretary) before defecting to Reform in January of this year.
The foreign donor cap is currently set at £100,000. There are no restrictions on how much citizens living in the UK can give parties. But if a Brit returning to the UK wishes to give more, the new law states that they need to be living in the country for a full calendar year before they can do so.
The issue with the laws perhaps applying retrospectively (i.e. from March) is that this could rule out these £36m a-piece donations from Harborne and Delo, as both of these crypto-billionaires have been living outside of the UK, and Reform may have to return the money.
Jenrick says in the case of Harborne, he won’t go into his personal circumstances but, “even if that were the case, the donation that he’s made would still be a legal one in compliance with the law. So we see no reason why you’d have to return these.”
Over on Sky, Conservative Tom Tugendhat was asked if the Tories were “rattled” by the money going into Reform.
He says he “welcomes people supporting political activity” in a democracy- at this point, Sky’s Rachel Johnson cuts in – “even crypto billionaires who live in Thailand?” (referring to Harborne).
Tugendhat then switches to his second point – the persistent murkiness over where Reform’s funds come from.
He raises the issue of due diligence, noting it’s a legal requirement for each party to rigorously check the sources of their donations and highlights that Reform has faced allegations this past week after a Channel 4 undercover investigation appeared to show Farage’s senior aides attempting to circumvent the rules to accept an otherwise illegal injection of foreign funding.
(Reform denies the allegations but Farage’s chief of staff and head of policy have stepped down and Labour has asked police to investigate possible offences. The Electoral Commission is also considering the allegations.)
Tugendhat goes on to argue that regardless of these donations and huge sums, “British people can’t be bought” and it’s an “illusion” to buy influence in public office.
He then also notes that these tens of millions have come from the crypto industry – noting that it’s the currency commonly used for laundering and to get around sanctions on foreign regimes like Russia and Iran.

Jenrick says donations 'breakthrough moment' for party

Good morning and welcome to the Guardian’s politics live blog in what is a fairly tumultuous period in electoral financing.

But it has also further muddied the reputation around the party’s finances and who it says it serves. There are also calls now across the political spectrum for a cap on donations from big-moneyed donors in the UK, a restriction that currently only applies to foreign donors.
