New artwork adorns Swiss Abroad Square on Lake Lucerne
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:05:59 UTC
17:05:59 KST

New artwork adorns Swiss Abroad Square on Lake Lucerne
The installation, which was unveiled on Saturday afternoon at Auslandschweizerplatz (Swiss Abroad Square) in Brunnen, central Switzerland, is called The Sun. It was created by Ugo Rondinone, an internationally acclaimed artist originally from Brunnen.
The work was commissioned by the Auslandschweizerplatz Foundation to enhance the 5,400-square-metre site on Lake LucerneExternal link. Rondinone used driftwood from the lake as his primary material.
The artist installed the circular structure in the meadow directly in front of the promenade. Looking through The Sun, one can see Lake Lucerne and the surrounding hills – the installation thus thrives on the direct view of nature.
More
The Swiss Abroad in nine charts
In Rondinone, the Auslandschweizerplatz Foundation was able to secure the services of an internationally renowned artist. Rondinone’s extraordinary commitment and his connection to his homeland were what made the project possible in the first place, canton Schwyz stated ahead of the opening.
The conceptual and installation artist Ugo Rondinone was born in 1964 to Italian immigrant parents and grew up in Brunnen. He studied in Vienna and now lives and works in Zurich and New York.
+ Swissinfo stories about the Swiss Abroad
Rondinone is famous for his stone figures. His oversized, majestic ‘stone men’ were exhibited at Rockefeller Plaza in New York in 2013. His ‘Seven Magic Mountains’ – a group of colourful stone figures – became a major attraction in the Nevada desert. A seven-metre-high stone figure by Rondinone is located nearby, in Andermatt, Uri.
The Auslandschweizerplatz was created in 1991 to mark the 700th anniversary of the Swiss Confederation. It marks the end of the “Path of Switzerland”, which runs around Lake Uri, and is intended to symbolise the affiliation of the Swiss Abroad to Switzerland.

Turkey unearths rare statues of Roman Emperor Hadrian, Empress Sabina in ancient Mediterranean city
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:01:39 UTC
17:01:39 KST

Nearly 2,000-year-old statues of Roman Emperor Hadrian and his wife, Empress Sabina, have been restored after being unearthed at the ancient city of Kibyra, Turkey’s Council of Higher Education (YOK) announced in late August.
Kibyra, located in southwest Turkey on the Mediterranean coast, came under Roman rule as part of the province of Asia in 133 BCE, following the Roman Republic's annexation of the Attalid Kingdom.
The two statues were among four discovered in recent excavations to uncover one of the city's key structures, the Monumental City Gate, spearheaded by a team from Burdur Mehmet Akif Ersoy University (MAKU).
Standing at a height of approximately 2.14 meters after restoration, Hadrian’s statue is made of high-quality marble taken from the Afyon-Iscehisar region.
The statue’s portrait confirmed that it belonged to Hadrian, making it an important, rare example of depictions of the emperor found in Anatolia, explained MAKU Professor and Kibyra Excavation Director Dr. Sukru Ozudogru.
Total of 20 statue fragments found at site
Ozudogru explained that the statues are thought to have been carved around 130 CE, in the midst of Hadrian’s reign.
He added that they may have been commissioned ahead of a visit by Hadrian to the region, as was common practice in the Roman period.
Hadrian’s statue is depicted wearing military garb, with the features of a lion and eagle carved into the emperor’s armor.
The statue of Sabina, while standing at the same height as Hadrian’s statue, is not as complete and is still missing fragments that archaeologists are hoping to uncover in future excavations.
An additional armored emperor statue, standing at roughly 1.86 meters tall; a female statue whose upper and lower body were found in two separate pieces; and a 30-centimeter-tall male statue head were also found at the gate dig site.
All four statues are thought to have been displayed on the upper part of the gate and have already been found at the gate,
Özüdoğru said, explaining that they had likely shattered after falling during the earthquake of 417 CE.
Once the four statues have been restored as completely as possible, they will be carefully transported and put on display at the Burdur Museum.
Twenty statue fragments, including arms, legs, and feet, have been unearthed in total during excavations in the city.
Notably, a bust of the Graeco-Egyptian deity Serapis and a statue of Asclepius, the Greek god of medicine, were found in 2019. A year later, an additional statue of Asclepius and the head of a bust of Serapis were found as well.
Over 2,000 blocks moved since start of excavations
Ozudogru noted that excavations on the gate, which has since antiquity collapsed into a pile of blocks, began in 2025.
Since, about 2,500 blocks have since been moved and taken in for classification and cataloguing.
According to him, the team will be able to complete excavations of the structure in one more season, and then the project could move forward into the formal restoration and redesign of the ancient gateway.
"These efforts also allow us to better understand Anatolia's history and the interaction between different civilizations throughout time,” said YOK President Erol Ozvar. “We consider it extremely important that our universities contribute to uncovering our history and cultural heritage through scientific research, and that they pass on these values to future generations by preserving them."

Chalet-style stations shape Switzerland's image
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
08:00:00 UTC
17:00:00 KST

Chalet-style stations shape Switzerland’s image
From Valais to Graubünden, via the Bernese Oberland and Gruyère, chalet-style railway stations help to shape the country’s picture-postcard image. First built in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, during the golden age of the railways, they have since followed varied paths. An exhibition is currently dedicated to them in Valais.
Let’s start with a basic question. Is the chalet to Switzerland what chocolate and watches are? “Yes,” replies Christophe Goumand. The Valais-based archaeologist and historian knows what he’s talking about, given that his father’s family were born and raised in a chalet. And not just any chalet. Not an Alpine chalet or a luxury holiday home, but a railway stop. In other words, a “gare-chalet”, a railway stop where passengers could board and alight.
“My grandfather was a railway maintenance worker responsible for maintaining the tracks at Finhaut station (canton Valais). The station was not a stone building but a wooden chalet, where his family lived. That was in the 1930s. There was another chalet station in the municipality of Finhaut: Châtelard-Village, run by a private company. When the operator wanted to demolish it, my grandfather – who was retiring at the time but still felt attached to the railway world – told him: ‘Don’t demolish it; I’ll take it.’ With the help of a contractor, he dismantled the wooden structure of the Châtelard station and reassembled it not far away, in Giétroz. Once moved there, this chalet became our holiday home. As a child, I used to go there often.”
Attracting English tourists
This personal journey explains Goumand’s fascination with chalet-style railway stations, to which he has dedicated an exhibition that runs until September 13 at the Galerie Victoria in Finhaut. Original plans, scale models, and old and recent photographs are on display for visitors to admire. As well as the history of the Swiss chalet, documented in the exhibition, visitors can explore the architecture of the wooden stations dotted along the Martigny–Châtelard line in the Trient Valley (Valais). Operated by a private railway company, Transports Martigny et Régions (TMR), it is now a “protected” line.
“This means it cannot be demolished,” explains the archaeologist.
Chalet-style stations also dot the landscapes of Gruyère, the Bernese Oberland, Graubünden and the Lake Geneva Riviera. “Some of them belong to the Swiss Federal Railways, such as the Vaud stations at Gland, Coppet and Roche. The latter was recently restored by the Federal Railways,” says Goumand.
Whether privately or publicly owned, most of them are still in service. They have existed since the late 19th and early 20th centuries and form part of Switzerland’s railway heritage. Their construction was once driven by a desire to attract English tourists, who were, at the time, very keen on Alpine holidays in the heart of a romantic Switzerland.
Rousseau and the romanticism of the chalet
“To my knowledge, there is no equivalent to these chalet-style stations anywhere else in Europe. In France, for example, there are some, but they are wooden houses; they do not have the same heritage value as ours,” says Goumand.
He goes on to highlight the role played by Jean-Jacques Rousseau in the idealisation of the beauty of the Swiss Alps. It was indeed the Genevan writer and philosopher who, in his novel La Nouvelle Héloïse (published in 1761), gave the chalet a prominent place as a setting for idyllic contemplation. Swiss engineers in the late 19th century were quick to recognise the chalet concept as an opportunity to export the image of an idyllic Switzerland and to reap significant profits from it.
Showcasing the expertise of Swiss carpenters
With the advent of the railways in the 19th century, railway stations flourished alongside the construction of chalets, which would become stopping points for trains. At the time, Swiss builders succeeded in exporting prefabricated chalets to France, taking advantage of the 1889 Paris World’s Fair to showcase their expertise. “Their approach proved successful. It’s worth noting that the Swiss Confederation, then in its infancy, promoted the talent of its carpenters at major exhibitions,” notes Goumand.
As a result, wealthy European families commissioned chalets to be installed on their vast estates. Prefabricated buildings, which also emerged in the 19th century, were highly sought after. Among the buyers was Charles Dickens, who owned a chalet on the outskirts of London. “It still stands today, amidst modern buildings; it was where the British author used to write,” says Goumand.
More
‘The chalet is the first prefab house in history’
The fate of chalet-style stations
Back in Switzerland, Goumand recounts an unusual anecdote about the chalet station known as the “three towns” station. It belongs to the public transport company Travys and “takes its name from its location, which offers views of Yverdon-les-Bains (Vaud), Estavayer-le-Lac (Fribourg) and Orbe (Vaud)”. Originally built to house railway maintenance workers, it has been let since 1990. Nowadays, the train that passes through stops only for the station’s sole tenant.
Every chalet station has its own fate. Klosters-Dorf, in Graubünden, which opened in 1889, has become a café and bakery. Trains still stop there, but this station no longer provides any services. Stationmasters have long since disappeared. Today, everything is automated. Modern stations? “Ah!” says Goumand, “they’re all the same all over the world – just copy and paste, nothing but concrete!” Nostalgic, then? “Yes and no – I remain realistic; you have to move with the times.”

The UN nuclear watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) brokered a local ceasefire last month to allow repairs and restore external power.
IAEA has stationed an observer team permanently at the station, along with Ukraine's three other working plants.
The agency has repeatedly acted as an intermediary when disputes arise and last month brokered a local ceasefire in order to carry out repairs and restore external power links.
Zaporizhzhia, Europe’s largest nuclear power plant with six reactors, currently generates no electricity.
Russian forces seized the plant in the early weeks of the war, which began in February 2022. Both sides have regularly accused each other of endangering safety at the site and increasing the risk of a nuclear accident.
Ukraine has demanded that Russia withdraw from the plant and return its operation to Kiev, a demand Moscow has rejected.

Iran loses ground in Hormuz as Houthis put Saudi Arabia under pressure
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:50:22 UTC
16:50:22 KST

Iran reported that an Iranian commercial vessel was hit early Sunday off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. One person was killed and three others were wounded. Earlier, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported that a vessel had been struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting the strait.
After nearly seven months of war, at varying levels of intensity, the United States appears in recent weeks to have succeeded in breaking Iran's grip on the Strait of Hormuz while nearly bringing Iranian oil exports to a complete halt, according to The Associated Press. That is expected to accelerate the country's economic decline. At least, that is what U.S. President Donald Trump hopes.
But the war launched by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28 — and which was intended to last only a few weeks — remains far from over, and the stalemate is exacting a heavy price on both sides. An agreement reached in June quickly collapsed, and there has been no diplomatic progress since. Low-intensity fighting continues, and the United States still appears to lack a clear exit strategy.
The growing economic pressure on Iran has yet to spark an uprising, and if its leaders are pushed into a corner, they could opt for military escalation rather than capitulation. At the same time, the Houthis, Iran's proxies in Yemen, have stepped up attacks against Saudi Arabia, driving oil prices higher again, and captured the strategic city of Al-Mokha on the Red Sea coast, giving them control over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Trump has acknowledged that gasoline prices are likely to remain high at least through the November midterm elections.
"Unfortunately, the U.S. is not winning in the war with Iran despite its limited success in loosening Iran’s grip over the strait and the devastating impact on Iran’s economy," Mona Yacoubian, a Middle East expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, told AP.
"Iran shows no sign of backing down and instead has demonstrated that it is prepared not only to fight back but to escalate wherever it can. The war is likely to drag on, with no clear winner."
Has Iran lost its leverage?
Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz — through which a fifth of the world's traded oil and gas passed before the war — in the opening days of the conflict, using the damage to the global economy as leverage. At the same time, it continued exporting its own oil, primarily to China.
In recent weeks, the balance of power appeared to shift. The U.S. blockade has nearly brought Iranian oil exports to a complete halt, while the U.S. military has helped Gulf states increase their exports. But in recent days, an escalation on another front could lead to another significant development in the complex conflict.
The tightening blockade and new U.S. sanctions are already taking a heavy toll on Iran's economy, driving up prices and creating even longer lines at gas stations. So far, however, the pressure has not led Iran's leaders to offer concessions over the Strait of Hormuz, its nuclear program or its support for proxies across the region.
Iran continues to attack ships in the strait, prompting limited U.S. strikes on its coastal areas, followed by Iranian retaliation in the form of missile attacks on Arab countries hosting U.S. forces.
At the same time, the Houthis this week launched a wave of attacks on Saudi oil facilities as part of a conflict that has lasted more than a decade but has escalated in recent weeks.
Saudi Arabia has few options
The Houthis' rapid advance threatens the main shipping route through the Red Sea. Against the backdrop of the complicated situation in Hormuz, drone attacks attributed to pro-Iranian militias operating in Iraq led to the closure of a major oil pipeline running across the kingdom. It is a nightmare scenario for Saudi Arabia, and it has already sent shock waves through markets around the world.
The Saudis' most important ally, on which they have long relied, was described by AP as unpredictable and, at times, unreliable. Trump appears reluctant to expand a war that is hurting his popularity and that of the Republican Party ahead of the congressional elections. For Iran, the rebels' advance and the shutdown of the oil pipeline increase the global economic pressure generated by the conflict.
Michael Ratney, a former U.S. ambassador to Saudi Arabia, said the latest developments are “incredibly frustrating” for the kingdom.
“Despite their antipathy for the Iranians, this is a war they had never asked for, they had great trepidation about. And once it started, all of their … worst-case scenarios started coming true.”
Until now, Saudi Arabia has managed to avoid some of the worst consequences of the war in the Gulf by pumping its oil across the Arabian Peninsula to the Red Sea. From there, it can be exported to Europe through Egypt via the SUMED pipeline and the Suez Canal, or to Asia along a route through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and onward to the Indian Ocean.
But tensions with the Houthis flared again in July, leading the rebels to declare a blockade of Saudi ships and resume large-scale attacks against them for the first time in four years. Over the past two days, the Houthis have seized the port city of Al-Mokha and an island in the Red Sea, significantly improving their ability to block Saudi oil shipments through Bab el-Mandeb.
Saudi Arabia said Friday that it had shut down the oil pipeline carrying crude from major oil fields in the country's east to the Red Sea in the west following drone attacks launched from Iraq. Regional officials recently told AP that the Houthis had helped Iraqi militias carry out the attacks.
Saudi Arabia fought the Houthis beginning in 2015, but its allies made little progress on the ground. The conflict killed about 150,000 people and pushed Yemen to the brink of famine before a ceasefire was reached in 2022. The Houthis' latest gains are increasing pressure on Riyadh to respond, but all the options available to it carry significant costs and uncertain outcomes.
Saudi Arabia could step up its own attacks and try to push back the Houthis, but that would prolong the confrontation and lead to heavier Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. It is a course the kingdom has pursued before, but the Houthis now possess more sophisticated weapons than they did in the past, while the Saudis likely have fewer interceptor missiles following the U.S.-Iran war.
The Saudis could also try to reach a diplomatic solution with the Houthis or their patrons in Tehran. But the Houthis are demanding an end to the Saudi-led blockade, which would allow them to grow significantly stronger over the long term, while Iran has little interest in stabilizing the region without securing major concessions from the United States.
Left to face the fight alone
For decades, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states have relied on U.S. security guarantees. Those guarantees have eroded under Trump, who also refrained from taking military action during his first term in response to a 2019 attack attributed to the Houthis that temporarily knocked out half of Saudi Arabia's oil production.
The United States began airstrikes against the Houthis in January 2024 under the Biden administration, and they continued until January 2025. Trump launched an air campaign against the rebels in March last year in response to attacks on ships in the Red Sea linked to the war in Gaza.
But U.S. forces are now deployed around the Strait of Hormuz, and the prolonged fighting has placed a significant strain on the U.S. military and depleted its stocks of advanced interceptor missiles.
The war is also unpopular in the United States and has eroded support for Trump after he promised to keep the country out of Middle East wars. Opening another military campaign in Yemen could further complicate matters for Republicans in closely contested House and Senate races.
Trump said Saturday that Iran was "probably" behind the attack on the Saudi oil pipeline. Asked about his recent conversation with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Trump said: "He's a good friend of mine, and all I can say is everything is going to work out great."

Turkish travel agencies raise concern over porposed online booking rules
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:48:06 UTC
16:48:06 KST

AA Photo
Turkish travel agencies have raised concerns over a draft law regulating international online accommodation platforms.
The legislation, which is expected to be submitted to parliament in the coming days, would establish a legal framework for foreign digital accommodation platforms operating in Türkiye.
Hasan Eker, vice chairman of the Association of Turkish Travel Agencies (TÜRSAB), said Turkish travel agencies currently operate under an overall tax burden of around 25 percent, while foreign online platforms would face a 5 percent tax rate under the proposed framework.
Eker argued that the difference in taxation could give online platforms a pricing advantage.
According to Eker, consumers could increasingly shift their reservations to foreign online platforms if those companies are able to offer lower prices as a result of their lower tax burden. He warned that such a trend could lead to a sharp decline in sales for Turkish travel agencies, weakening competition and increasing the risk of market concentration.
“If monopolization occurs, they will start determining prices themselves,” Eker said, adding that such a scenario could eventually result in platforms purchasing rooms from hotels at lower prices and selling them to consumers at higher prices.
Eker said the association’s main demand is equal treatment under Turkish regulations.
“We want citizens to receive services through Booking [booking. com]. Our issue is that Booking does not have an office in the country,” he said. “Foreign digital platforms operating in Türkiye should be subject to the same obligations as domestic travel agencies.”
Under the draft legislation, foreign digital accommodation platforms will be required to obtain a permit from the Culture and Tourism Ministry in order to operate in Türkiye.
The draft also requires foreign platforms, including Booking, to maintain a local representative in Türkiye.

Türkiye to expand EV charging network in clean transport push
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:46:21 UTC
16:46:21 KST

Türkiye plans to accelerate the rollout of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure nationwide as part of its Medium-Term Program (OVP), which includes measures to support cleaner transportation and reduce emissions.
Under the program, the government will finalize and implement the “Net Zero Emissions Strategy and Action Plan for Transportation.” Authorities will also prepare a technology roadmap for integrated, efficient, safe and environmentally friendly intelligent transportation systems and launch projects aimed at reducing transport-related emissions, improving sustainability and enhancing connectivity.
The program calls for the nationwide expansion of EV charging stations. In addition, a national plan will be prepared to support the electrification of heavy commercial vehicles in the logistics sector through the deployment of high-capacity charging infrastructure.
The move comes as growth in Türkiye’s electric vehicle fleet continues to outpace the expansion of charging infrastructure.
According to July 2026 data from the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EPDK), the number of EVs on Turkish roads reached nearly 465,000, while the number of commercially operated public charging sockets stood at 46,665.
As a result, there were about 10 electric vehicles per public charging socket, compared with roughly eight EVs per charging point on average in the European Union.
The number of EVs in Türkiye stood at around 300,000 in July 2025, highlighting the rapid pace of adoption over the past year.
The country’s EV charging network reached a total installed capacity of 3,677 MW (3.68 GW) as of July 2026, up from 2,374 MW a year earlier.

how domestic work became built into the floor plan of the modern home
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:45:47 UTC
16:45:47 KST

Most houses have a room whose only purpose is to get you somewhere else. Most of us are so used to the idea of the hallway that it’s hard to imagine it was ever novel. Yet for much of architectural history, especially in large European villas, movement worked differently. Rooms were organized as a cluster so that they each opened directly into each other.
In Palladian villas for instance, aligned doorways could turn a sequence of interiors into a continuous route, which meant crossing the house also meant crossing spaces where other people were already sitting or eating, sleeping or receiving guests.
Architectural historian Robin Evans made the corridor famous as a clue to a much larger change in domestic planning. In his 1978 essay Figures, Doors and Passages, he pointed to John Thorpe’s plan for Beaufort House in Chelsea, drawn around 1597, as an early recorded English example in which a central passage gave rooms independent access.
Even the word carries movement inside it: corridor comes through Italian corridore, linked to correre, ‘to run.’ A strip of space devoted almost entirely to getting from one place to another seems simple now. At the time, it changed what a room could be.
Villa Thiene, Andrea Palladio, Vicenza, Italy, 16th-century
privacy arrived with another route through the house
Once movement could be pulled out of occupied rooms, the plan could begin separating one kind of presence from another. A household member could remain in a parlor while someone crossed the building through a passage nearby.
By the nineteenth century, wealthy houses developed parallel systems of circulation, with back stairs and service passages moving domestic workers around the edges of family spaces. Rooms could be supplied with reduced encounters, meaning privacy could be produced in plan.
Even though the class structure behind those houses is specific, the spatial idea crossed over into middle-class houses and even apartments. Utility rooms absorbed recurring household tasks, and rear entrances created another way for groceries or deliveries to enter.
The people performing domestic work changed, and in many homes the resident took on work once assigned to staff. Still, the floor plan kept many of the same habits.
MOS Architects turned that inherited logic inside out with House No. 11, or Corridor House, built for the inaugural Chicago Architecture Biennial in 2015. The installation is assembled from narrow modules based roughly on the dimensions of a conventional corridor and a sheet of plywood. A bed appears inside one. A desk occupies another.
The passage, usually treated as the neutral leftover between destinations, becomes the destination itself. MOS described the corridor as a device that made architecture increasingly concerned with circulation, with getting people and goods from one place to another faster. Their house occupies that circuitry and asks what happens when the supposedly empty strip acquires a life of its own.
Taku Sakaushi and OFDA’s Three Corridors House in Japan approaches the same question through a lived domestic plan. A long central hallway crosses the single-story house, while slimmer passages along the north and south edges double as verandas. Bathrooms and storage settle into the areas created between them. Study space appears there too.
Circulation becomes a framework that organizes the entire interior, yet those corridors are wide enough and exposed enough to acquire other uses. The project makes visible a strange fact about the conventional hallway: a space developed to prevent interruption can become one of the most social parts of a house once architecture stops treating it as wasted area.
Some of the clearest examples appear in spaces associated with maintenance. In Fala Atelier’s House Within Three Gestures in Gondomar, Portugal, the laundry room breaks away from the main volume and rises into a small tower. It’s an unuaual move, but it’s also a revealing one.
While laundry usually gets tucked behind a door or squeezed into a closet, here it’s one of the house’s most work-oriented rooms and changes the silhouette of the whole building. A function that architecture has spent centuries pushing toward the edge suddenly gets its own vertical figure.
Mesura’s Vasto Gallery in Barcelona makes this dependency easy to read. The converted industrial apartment is organized around a freestanding wooden service core, detached from the surrounding walls and ceiling. An eight-meter stainless-steel kitchen counter stretches openly through the main room, while private functions gather around the central volume.
The old hierarchy between front room and service room becomes harder to maintain when both are treated as major spatial elements. The mechanisms of living sit in plain sight.
A-01’s No Footprint House in Costa Rica compresses domestic systems into one central service core, leaving the plan open around it. Utilities gather at the center while the rest of the house remains adaptable. It is a contemporary version of an old architectural instinct: collect the work somewhere specific so the surrounding space can feel free.
Here, this work extends to energy and climate control as much as it does cleaning or cooking. Domestic labor has expanded into building services, and architecture still gives those services their own territory.
the ordinary plan is full of architectural fossils
Look again at an ordinary house and these divisions start to appear everywhere. The hallway lets one person cross the home without crossing another person’s room. The laundry closet contains a repeating cycle of work behind two doors. A garage entrance receives shoes and bags before they travel farther inside.
Even the mechanical cupboard is a tiny sealed room devoted to the systems that make every other room comfortable. These spaces rarely define how a home is described, although the home would struggle to function without them.
The interesting part is how long these arrangements survive after their original social conditions shift. A corridor that once helped separate servants from employers becomes the hallway in a two-bedroom apartment. A service zone becomes the utility core of an experimental house, and a laundry room becomes a tower. Architecture keeps old behaviors longer than we tend to realize.
This article is part of designboom’s MODES OF HABITATION chapter, exploring how the spaces we inhabit can reshape the ways we live together. Discover more stories rethinking domesticity, shared living, and the many forms a home can take here.

PM Modi welcomed the “steady progress” in relations but underlined that peace and tranquillity in border areas would remain an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral ties.The meeting was the leaders’ third bilateral interaction in two years, following their meetings in Kazan in 2024 and Tianjin last year. It was also their first meeting on Indian soil in seven years.Xi reiterated that India and China were partners, not rivals. However, the Indian readout did not include that formulation.Also read: Why Xi Jinping skipped PM Modi’s gala dinner at Brics Summit in Delhi
Border, trade issues on agenda
PM Modi stressed the need for both sides to honour existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.The Indian side said the leaders reaffirmed their commitment to finding a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution to the boundary question, keeping in mind the broader political perspective of bilateral ties and the long-term interests of both countries.Modi also raised India’s trade deficit with China and called for greater predictability in supply chains and meaningful, predictable market access.The two sides discussed the need to address concerns related to structural trade imbalances, supply chains and economic cooperation.Since the 2024 Kazan meeting, which marked the end of the eastern Ladakh border standoff, three rounds of talks between the Special Representatives of India and China have taken place. At their latest meeting, the two sides agreed to work towards an early and substantial outcome on boundary delimitation and border management.

Xi skips gala dinner
Xi Jinping, however, did not attend a gala dinner hosted by PM Modi for Brics leaders, partner countries and representatives of international organisations, sources aware of the matter told PTI.The reason for his absence was not immediately known. A source suggested that Xi had returned to his hotel to rest after a busy day.Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, who left for home after attending the summit, was also absent from the dinner.Russian President Vladimir Putin and other Brics leaders attended the event. Union ministers, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and several chief ministers were also present.Union ministers at the dinner included Amit Shah, Nirmala Sitharaman, Piyush Goyal, Ashwini Vaishnaw and Shivraj Singh Chouhan. Chief ministers Yogi Adityanath, Devendra Fadnavis, Suvendu Adhikari and Himanta Biswa Sarma also attended.
The ministers and chief ministers travelled in two buses from Parliament House to Bharat Mandapam, where the dinner was held.The dinner menu featured khandvi mille-feuille, khumb galouti, paneer lababdar, gucchi marmik, carrot-bean poriyal and millet pulao.The dessert menu included Old Delhi fruit cream with jalebi and shahtoot phirni. Pezeshkian warns against unilateral sanctions at BRICS summit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:38:38 UTC
16:38:38 KST

Speaking at the 18th BRICS Plus summit, Pezeshkian said no country can solve today's global challenges alone. "BRICS must turn the scattered capacities of Global South countries into shared capacity. Iran's geopolitical position and its energy and transit capacities can play an effective role in developing trade and energy routes among members," he said.
 
 
 He said resilience means having the capacity to maintain the path of development and independent decision-making even under pressure. Excessive dependence on limited financial and trade systems makes economies vulnerable to political shocks. "Today, unilateral sanctions are not merely an economic issue; they directly affect food security and people's welfare. Therefore, BRICS must build shared capacity for members' economic resilience by developing trade in national currencies and strengthening the New Development Bank."
 
 
 Pezeshkian said economic resilience without security will not be sustainable. Developments in the region, especially the U.S. and Israeli military aggression against Iran, showed that the effects of targeting a country's economic, energy and development infrastructure quickly transcend its borders and bring regional and global consequences.
 
 
 "The Iranian people have paid a heavy price for these aggressions. Men and women, children and civilians have lost their lives, and infrastructure built over decades for the country's development has been damaged. These events remind us of the heavy responsibility of the international community to protect civilians and prevent the normalisation of attacks on civilian targets," he said.
 
 
 He said the people of Gaza and Lebanon continue to face the consequences of crimes and genocide. "One cannot speak of international law if there is no effective international response to military aggression, the killing of people and the destruction of their lives. Therefore, BRICS must play a more effective role in defending national sovereignty, territorial integrity and the prohibition of the use of force."
 
 
 Pezeshkian identified cooperation as the second pillar. No country alone can solve today's global challenges, he said, and BRICS must turn scattered capacities into shared capability. Sustainability was the third pillar. "Development that increases inequality or places today's costs on future generations will not be sustainable. We must not forget that war is one of the serious causes of environmental destruction. Iran's recent experience showed that damage to energy and industrial infrastructure has consequences beyond economic loss and affects the region's natural resources."
 
 
 He said knowledge and innovation are also determining factors. "BRICS must ensure that artificial intelligence and new technologies do not become tools of domination but means of empowering nations."
 
 
 Pezeshkian said BRICS is no longer merely a framework for cooperation among emerging economies but a sign of growing demand for a more balanced and inclusive world in which no power centre has the right to determine the fate of others. Iran, he said, is ready to put its capacities at the service of BRICS cooperation.
 
 
 "Resilience without cooperation will not last, cooperation without justice is not sustainable, and sustainability without peace and security is not possible. Let us turn BRICS into a platform for converting these principles into practical action," he said.

Türkiye to boost mining investment to strengthen energy security
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:36:10 UTC
16:36:10 KST

AA Photo
Türkiye will increase investments in mining and domestic resource development to strengthen energy security under its 2027-2029 Medium-Term Program (OVP).
According to the program, the country will enhance exploration, production and value-added utilization of domestic resources, diversify energy supplies, expand storage capacity and strengthen local production and research capabilities in critical minerals, energy and mining technologies.
As part of these efforts, regulatory changes will be introduced to reduce import dependency on critical and strategic minerals and support domestic production.
Türkiye will also conduct research and development activities in clean coal technologies, including coal gasification, carbon capture and storage and advanced carbon products.
R&D and product development projects aimed at localizing critical technologies and equipment used in the energy and mining sectors will be supported. The government also plans to expand the production and sales of high value-added boron products and accelerate the economic utilization of rare earth elements.
İbrahim Halil Kırşan, head of the Mining Council of the Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Türkiye (TOBB), welcomed the planned increase in exploration spending by the General Directorate of Mineral Research and Exploration (MTA).
“The 139 percent increase in MTA exploration investments included under additional funding for strategic priorities is highly appropriate for unlocking our country’s mining potential,” Kırşan said.
He added that the government’s goal of increasing oil, natural gas and mineral exploration and production both domestically and abroad, while generating greater value from reserves, demonstrated the strategic importance attached to the mining sector.
“This approach signals a significant shift in mindset for our industry,” Kırşan said.
Kırşan noted that although Türkiye possesses strong mineral resources and a well-established mining culture, its capacity to process, refine and transform minerals into advanced technology products remains limited.
“As a result, a large share of the value added is created abroad,” he said.
At the same time, Kırşan said Türkiye’s growing domestic manufacturing base in the energy transition, automotive and defense industries has the potential to generate substantial demand for processed critical minerals.
“Türkiye’s competitive advantage lies not only in its geological potential but also in the combination of its industrial capacity, logistics network and geopolitical position,” he said.

Premier Cho officiates at mass wedding in Taipei
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:35:56 UTC
16:35:56 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) officiated at a mass wedding for 72 couples at the Grand Hotel on Sunday, urging the newlyweds to be tolerant, considerate, and trusting as they begin their lives together.
Cho said marriage is an important milestone and expressed hope that the couples would continue their journey together and make a lifelong commitment to building families. The ceremony was held as the government promotes its new population strategy, which aims to provide greater support for people at the stages of childbirth, child-rearing, and education, per a Cabinet press release.
Cho joked that although he regularly signs large numbers of documents as premier, he had never been as happy to serve as an officiant. Among the 72 couples participating in the Chunghwa Telecom group wedding, five had both partners working for the telecommunications company.
During the ceremony, the grooms knelt on one knee and presented rings to their brides after instructions from the master of ceremonies. The couples then exchanged vows as family members and guests looked on.
Cho said this was his first time attending a corporate mass wedding since the government announced its new population strategy. He stressed that marriage is an important life choice and that having children is a personal decision rather than a responsibility or obligation.
“Marriage is everyone's right, and having children is everyone's choice,” Cho said, adding that starting a family can bring major changes to people's lives. The government's new population strategy focuses on five areas: supporting childbirth, strengthening child care, increasing educational support, creating family-friendly workplaces, and easing housing pressures.
Cho said the government plans to introduce a monthly NT$5,000 (US$158) growth allowance for children from birth until age 18 beginning in 2027. Under the proposed system, half of the monthly allowance for children from age 6 until 18 would be placed in a government-managed growth account.
He encouraged the newlyweds to make use of government support if they decide to have children. He said the government also plans to expand affordable child care services nationwide as part of the population strategy.
Cho thanked Chunghwa Telecom for establishing 10 workplace child care centers with a total of 18 classes. The company says the centers are located in the six special municipalities and provide child care near employees' workplaces, reducing the difficulty of balancing work and family responsibilities.
Cho also praised Chunghwa Telecom for its family-friendly employment policies. The company currently provides 91 days of maternity leave, compared with the statutory eight weeks, as well as 10 days each of prenatal examination leave and paternity leave. It also provides employees with children under age 6 the option of reducing working hours by one hour per day without affecting pay or other labor rights.
Cho additionally praised Chunghwa Telecom's technological development, saying the company is preparing for the transition from current 4G and 5G networks toward 6G. He said this was important as Taiwan pursues greater AI adoption.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Patients with minor illnesses or injuries could have a weekday alternative to National Taiwan University Hospital's emergency department under plans for a nearby urgent care center.
Monday and Tuesday sessions are under consideration for a proposed facility at Huashan Market, with hours tailored to NTU Hospital's busiest periods, per UDN.
Taiwan's 13 existing centers serve six major cities, treating minor injuries, digestive and respiratory symptoms, and fever, mainly now on national holidays and Sundays. The National Health Insurance Administration began an adjusted program last November.
Health ministry Medical Affairs Director Liu Yueh-ping (劉越萍) said the first month or two of clinic operations could guide staffing and scheduling adjustments, according to the report. No target has been set for how many patients the facility should divert.
The ministry expects further talks with the hospital in late September, ahead of Taipei's hoped-for October opening. Operating arrangements, the site, and space preparations remain unsettled.
NTU Hospital came under scrutiny last month when a patient died after waiting 12 days in emergency care for an inpatient bed.
Liu said the ministry is tracking bed turnover and the proportion of emergency patients admitted to the hospital, emphasizing that overcrowding cannot be solved with just one policy shift.
A separate effort to transfer emergency patients to wards remains pending while the hospital arranges staffing, per CNA.

Zelenskyy Says He Is Ready to Meet Putin at December G20 Summit in Miami
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he is prepared to attend the G20 summit in Miami in December and meet Russian leader Vladimir Putin there if Putin also takes part in the gathering.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
In an interview with Deutsche Welle conducted on September 11 at the Canadian Forces Base North Bay, Zelenskyy said a face-to-face meeting should focus on reaching concrete decisions rather than exchanging statements.
“Yes, of course. We have to come. We have to meet, talk and make decisions,” Zelenskyy said when asked whether he would be willing to meet Putin at the summit. The Ukrainian president added that the substance of any potential meeting would be measured by its outcome.
“It does not matter what I tell him or what he wants to tell me. Only the result will matter. That is all,” Zelenskyy said. The G20 leaders’ summit in Miami is scheduled for December 14-15, 2026. Ukraine is currently not listed among the invited non-G20 countries on the summit’s official website.
It also remains unclear whether Putin will attend the meeting in person.
Zelenskyy has previously said that Ukraine, the US, and Russia could hold a trilateral meeting as early as this autumn. He said he first plans to meet US President Donald Trump in September, after which work could begin on organizing broader negotiations.
The Ukrainian president has named Switzerland, Türkiye, and the United Arab Emirates among possible venues for future trilateral talks, saying other countries have also offered to host negotiations. He has indicated that issues including energy and grain could be discussed.
Zelenskyy and Putin have not held direct talks since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Their only in-person meeting took place in Paris on December 9, 2019, during a Normandy Format summit involving Ukraine, Russia, France, and Germany. Zelenskyy and Putin held a brief bilateral meeting before wider negotiations between the Ukrainian and Russian delegations.
Earlier, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner discussed the possibility of a limited winter ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia, potentially including a mutual pause on strikes against energy infrastructure.

Estonia's next defense minister pick Herem has security experts concerned
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:27:00 UTC
16:27:00 KST

Estonia's next defense minister pick Herem has security experts concerned
Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) ex-chief Martin Herem's selection as Estonia's next defense minister has some defense experts troubled over industry ties and procurement plans.
Herem's move from the EDF to the Ministry of Defense is nothing unusual in itself, but retired Maj. Gen. Neeme Väli said the current process has lacked transparency. He is particularly concerned about Herem's direct ties to defense industry firm Frankenburg and the possibility that other people from the company could also return to government service.
"If Kusti Salm is to return to the Defense Ministry, he first has to be found," Väli said, referring to the ministry's former permanent secretary, named CEO of Frankenburg Technologies in fall 2024. "I don't know how that conflict of interest will be resolved or prevented, but we'll see how it goes."
He also noted that some of the issues facing Estonia's defense sector began while Herem was still among its decision-makers.
Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform), however, said he has no doubts about Herem's ability to address the ministry's problems.
"Martin Herem knows where he succeeded and where he failed," Michal said, adding that an outside partner should be brought in to help restore public trust in the sector.
Security expert Rainer Saks said Michal was taking a risk by placing such confidence in Herem. While the EDF's accounting can likely be brought into order, Saks said procurements remain the bigger concern.
"We have a rapidly growing defense budget, a lot of defense procurements and not enough people with experience doing this work and spending that money effectively," Saks said, adding that the pressure to move quickly compounds the problem.
Expert: Intelligence should guide policy
Väli likewise questioned the urgency surrounding Herem's plans, saying decisions on the pace of defense preparations should be based on intelligence assessments.
"What is this speed based on? It's based on Martin Herem's personal assessment," he said. "No intelligence assessment supports it today." He said professional intelligence should guide policy, not the other way around.
Väli also warned against hastily changing laws or procedures or granting the new defense minister special powers.
Michal said Herem has not requested such powers, only political backing for reforms and efforts to improve Estonia's defense capabilities. Herem also does not plan to join a political party.
Herem, who has been on vacation, is due back in Estonia Sunday.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday warned against the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals, saying that there is a need for inclusivity in the adoption of technology.During his closing remarks on the second day of the Brics summit, PM Modi said that tightening control over technology and critical minerals could hinder shared progress of countries.
"Under the umbrella of innovation, the Brics Incubator Network will connect our startups and incubators. We have proposed the Brics Startup Innovation Fund to promote innovative and scalable solutions. The Brics Network on Digital Agriculture will create new opportunities for farmers; through this initiative, AI, geospatial technology, and digital public infrastructure will be aligned with the actual needs of farmers. The weaponisation of technology and critical minerals could hinder our shared progress; therefore, we have emphasised inclusivity in the adoption of technology,” PM Modi said.“The strength of Brics lies in our diversity and cooperation. We may be rooted in different realities, but together we rise through cooperation and blossom for humanity. May our diversity remain our identity, our cooperation serve as our inspiration, and our progress benefit all of humanity," he added.
Interestingly, the remarks were made in the presence of Chinese President Xi Jinping. Although the Prime Minister did not name any particular country, the remarks can be seen as a message to Beijing, which holds a dominant position in global supply chains for critical minerals and rare earths.Last year, China tightened its export controls on rare earths and other materials critical for advanced tech manufacturing during trade negotiations with the United States.China controls more than 90 percent of global rare-earth refining, giving it enormous leverage over critical technologies, from the permanent magnets used in EVs and AI data centres to components in advanced electronics and semiconductors.During his address, PM Modi also said that “India has advanced the spirit of friendship, partnership, and cooperation through the Brics platform.”“We have endeavoured to ensure that Brics cooperation is not limited to governments alone; we want our entrepreneurs, farmers, researchers, women, youth, and ordinary citizens to become active participants as well,” PM Modi said.
"I can say from personal experience that the trust of Global South nations in Brics has grown, because their voices are heard, their experiences are respected, and solutions are crafted not just for them, but with them. The strength of Brics lies in our diversity and cooperation. We may be rooted in different realities, but together we rise through cooperation and blossom for humanity. May our diversity remain our identity, our cooperation serve as our inspiration, and our progress benefit all of humanity," he added.
The last leg of the summit focused on the core pillars of India's 2026 Brics chairship -- resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. The two-day summit is being hosted by India on September 12-13 under the chairship theme, “Building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability."The open session is part of the two-day Brics summit being hosted by India on September 12-13 under the chairship theme, “Building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability."

16:24:22 KST

SANAA, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Yemen's Houthi group said Sunday that it had launched a large-scale ballistic missile and drone attack on a military base in southern Saudi Arabia.
In a statement posted on X, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said the attack targeted weapons depots and command-and-control facilities at a military base in Sharurah, a Saudi city near the Yemeni border.
Sarea said a "large barrage" of ballistic missiles and drones was used, claiming the attack directly hit its targets. He gave no details on casualties or damage.
He said the operation was in retaliation for continued Saudi military action in Yemen and warned that further escalation would be met with "larger operations" deeper inside Saudi territory.
There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities on the claim.
The attack came amid a sharp escalation in Yemen, where intense fighting has spread across several fronts since the Houthis launched a major offensive on Sept. 3.
The Houthis have since made rapid gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast, capturing the strategic port city of Mocha on Thursday and expanding their control around the Bab al-Mandab Strait on Friday.
Yemen's conflict began in late 2014 when the Houthis seized Sanaa and much of northern Yemen, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene the following year in support of the internationally recognized government. ■

Netanyahu's Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar trade leads as 2026 election picture stays unclear - poll
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:22:49 UTC
16:22:49 KST

Five polls published after the Knesset candidate lists closed show a highly fragmented political landscape, with no clear advantage for either major bloc, Maariv reported on Sunday.
In four of the five surveys, Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party emerged as the largest party, while an i24NEWS poll showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud taking first place by a significant margin. Former IDF Brig.-Gen. Ofer Winter’s People of Israel party crossed the electoral threshold in all five polls, while Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha’s Economic Party only passed the threshold in the Kan News survey.
The bloc picture also remained unclear. Two polls showed an exact tie between the major blocs, while the others gave an advantage to the opposition bloc, with the exception of the i24NEWS poll, which showed a significant strengthening of Netanyahu’s bloc.
i24NEWS: Likud leads with 27 seats
The most notable poll of the week was conducted by i24NEWS and Direct Polls. Unlike all other surveys, it showed Netanyahu’s Likud leading the race with 27 seats, while Eisenkot’s Yashar received 22.
Naftali Bennett’s B’yachad declined to 10 seats, the Democrats received 9, United Torah Judaism and Otzma Yehudit each received 8, and the Joint List, Yisrael Beytenu, and Shas each received 7 seats.
The Religious Party and Zehut received 6 seats each, Ra’am received 5, and Ofer Winter’s People of Israel received 4 seats.
The reservists’ list and Hendel and Zelekha’s Economic Party remained far below the electoral threshold, receiving 1.4% and 1.1%, respectively. Blue and White received 1.1%.
According to the seat distribution, Netanyahu’s bloc together with Winter reaches 60 seats, the opposition bloc reaches 48, and the Arab parties hold 12 seats.
Channel 13: 53-53 tie
A Channel 13 poll presented a completely different picture, with Eisenkot’s Yashar receiving 22 seats while Netanyahu’s Likud fell to 19.
Bennett received 13 seats, Shas received 7, and Ofer Winter’s People of Israel received 4. Hendel and Zelekha received 3.2% and remained below the electoral threshold.
Benny Gantz’s Blue and White and the Haredi Public party also failed to enter the Knesset.
The bloc breakdown showed a complete tie, with Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition bloc each receiving 53 seats, while the Arab parties held the remaining 14 seats.
Kan News: Yashar leads with 25 seats
The Kan News poll also placed Eisenkot’s Yashar party in first place, with 25 seats. Netanyahu’s Likud received 21 seats, while Bennett’s B’yachad received 14.
The Democrats received 10 seats, Yisrael Beytenu and Otzma Yehudit each received 8, United Torah Judaism received 7, and the Joint List received 6.
The Religious Party, Shas, and Ofer Winter’s People of Israel each received 5 seats, while Hendel and Zelekha’s Economic Party also crossed the electoral threshold with 4 seats.
Blue and White, the reservists’ list, and other parties failed to enter the Knesset.
The bloc breakdown showed a narrow advantage for the opposition bloc, which reached 58 seats, compared with 50 seats for Netanyahu’s bloc. The Arab parties held 12 seats.
Channel 12: Yashar in the lead
A Channel 12 poll also placed Eisenkot’s Yashar as the largest party, with 24 seats. Likud received 22, B’yachad received 15, and the Democrats received 11.
Otzma Yehudit received 9 seats, Yisrael Beytenu received 8, United Torah Judaism and Shas each received 7, the Joint List received 6, and the Religious Party received 5.
People of Israel, led by Ofer Winter, received 4 seats and crossed the electoral threshold, while Hendel and Zelekha remained below it.
The bloc calculation gave Netanyahu’s bloc, including Winter, 54 seats, the opposition bloc 55 seats, and the Arab parties 11 seats.
Maariv: Tight race between blocs
The Maariv poll showed another close race, with Yashar receiving 24 seats and Likud receiving 23. B’yachad received 14 seats, the Democrats received 10, and Otzma Yehudit received 9.
Yisrael Beytenu and United Torah Judaism each received 8 seats, Shas received 7, the Joint List received 6, and the Religious Party received 5.
People of Israel received 5 seats, while Hendel and Zelekha’s party received 3.5% and remained below the electoral threshold.
According to the bloc breakdown, Netanyahu’s bloc reached 52 seats, the opposition bloc reached 52 seats, and the Arab parties held 16 seats.
Summary of the polling picture
The five polls paint a fragmented political landscape with no clear winner. Eisenkot’s Yashar party leads in most surveys, but the i24NEWS poll shows Netanyahu’s Likud returning to first place with a significant advantage.
Ofer Winter’s People of Israel consistently crosses the electoral threshold, while Hendel and Zelekha’s party only succeeds in the Kan News poll.
The overall picture remains one of a tight contest between Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition bloc, with Arab parties potentially holding the balance of power.

Putin says intra-BRICS trade reaches $1.2T
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:21:26 UTC
16:21:26 KST

Elena Teslova
13 September 2026•Update: 13 September 2026
Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Sunday that trade among BRICS countries has reached $1.2 trillion.
Speaking at a meeting of the BRICS Outreach format in New Delhi, Putin said that the population growth rates in the BRICS countries are increasing from year to year, domestic markets are strengthening, and infrastructure of all kinds has been built.
“Domestic trade within our association has already reached $1.2 trillion. The participating countries account for almost a quarter of global exports, and it is the BRICS that provides the main dynamics of global GDP – 49%,” he said.
Putin emphasized that the potential for further development of BRICS is “far from exhausted.”
“One of the main reserves that has not yet been fully utilized is the complementarity of the economies of the participating countries. Differences in their structure and specialization provide ample opportunities for practical cooperation, for the creation of new production chains, technologies, services and markets,” he said.
"In fact, we are talking about forming a common BRICS growth platform that organically combines the competitive advantages of our economies," Putin noted.
The Russian president added that attention to BRICS activities in the world continues to grow.
He said the group's values and ideals were becoming increasingly attractive, adding that BRICS advocates equal and unrestricted opportunities for all countries to achieve social and economic growth.
Putin also said the group was actively contributing to the formation of a more just multipolar world order.

Over 700 cardholders report unauthorised iPhone pre-order charges worth HK$14.7m
Some report multiple transactions on their credit cards, while an expert says fraudsters may have exploited pre-order rush for Apple’s new iPhones
Hong Kong police have received reports from more than 700 people regarding unauthorised transactions on credit cards worth HK$14.7 million (US$1.87 million) linked to pre-orders of Apple’s newest iPhones, prompting the force and major banks to launch investigations.
A police spokesman said the force’s e-Report Centre received the reports on Saturday and Sunday from individuals who suspected that their credit cards were fraudulently used for online purchases of smartphones. The largest single case involved as much as HK$114,000.
Following preliminary investigations, the cases have been provisionally classified as “obtaining property by deception”. No arrests have been made so far.
One social media user on the Threads platform said she received a message on Saturday night that she had unauthorised transactions of HK$33,598 from Apple on her HSBC credit card.
“When I called Apple customer service, they hung up on me immediately. What should I do?” she asked.
It took her half an hour to reach an HSBC customer service officer to suspend her credit card, and she subsequently filed a police report.

On Sept 12th, 'everyone was compassionate': The world needs 'to be together again' - Richard Roeill

On Sept 12th, 'everyone was compassionate': The world needs 'to be together again' - Richard Roeill
To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
Issued on: Modified:
François Picard is pleased to welcome Richard Roeill, former New York Firefighter and 9/11 First Responder. His testimony reframes the legacy of September 11th not as a historical event confined to a single day, but as living history. The former New York City firefighter describes an anniversary that reactivates trauma, while the illnesses suffered by first responders make the consequences of Ground Zero ever present decades later. Yet Roeill’s testimony is not simply a narrative of sacrifice. He says that responders were misled about the dangers they faced, demanding accountability and long-term healthcare for those exposed to the very toxic air.
At the same time, Roeill resists ending with anger. His memory of September 12 - when, in his telling, distinctions of race, religion and gender temporarily receded before a sense of common humanity - becomes both an ideal and an implicit critique of the present. What he ultimately asks viewers to remember, therefore, is not only what was lost on September 11, but what solidarity looked like immediately afterward, and what we owe those still living with its consequences.
His account moves between vulnerability and duty: declining lung capacity, the deaths of colleagues and the emotional burden of repeated funerals coexist with his striking insistence that, knowing what he knows now, he would still have responded exactly as he had done. "Absolutely. There's a lot of legacy firemen now, meaning that the ones that have passed from 9/11, that their kids are following in their footsteps, and it's a really wonderful thing. I got to witness about six months ago at Rescue 4. There were a few legacy children and firemen there, and it was great to see that they had great camaraderie, and they all stuck together because they had another bond that other people didn't. And it was really — it was beautiful to see, actually. It really was, knowing that they were there for each other and keeping their parents' legacies alive."

Russian Nuclear Head Says Ukraine Attacked Fuel Trucks, Endangered Zaporizhzhia Plant
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:17:03 UTC
16:17:03 KST

The head of Russia's state nuclear energy corporation accused Ukraine on Sunday of attacking diesel fuel trucks, killing two Russian servicemen and deliberately jeopardizing safety at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine.
Alexei Likhachev said the attack took place on Friday and also resulted in injuries to other Russian soldiers.
The Zaporizhzhia plant, Europe's largest with six reactors, was seized by Russian forces in the early weeks of the Ukraine war that broke out in February 2022. Each side has regularly accused the other of actions that endanger safety at the plant and increase the risk of a nuclear accident.
Likhachev issued a statement saying Ukrainian forces had launched “a series of combined strikes” on Friday on fuel trucks which deliver diesel to the station.
“The strikes hit very close to the perimeter of the station's site,” he said.
“Two servicemen were killed, and a large number of Russian soldiers were injured, some seriously. They were all involved in supporting this purely civilian mission.”
Fuel is critically important for the plant as diesel generators provide power to keep nuclear fuel in the reactors cool when the plant's two external power links are down. Both were down for nearly three weeks in August and September.
Ukraine has demanded that Russia abandon the station and hand its operation back to Kyiv, a demand rejected by Moscow. The fuel currently generates no electricity.
The UN nuclear watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency, has stationed an observer team permanently at the station, along with Ukraine's three other working plants.
The agency has repeatedly acted as an intermediary when disputes arise and last month helped arrange a local ceasefire in order to carry out repairs and restore external power links.
Russia Hits Truck Near Polish Border in Latest Strike Near NATO
Russia attacked a truck near Ukraine's border with Poland, Polish and Ukrainian officials said on Sunday, the latest strike to hit areas near NATO as Moscow and Kyiv intensify their long-distance strikes to try to shift momentum in the war.
Polish border guards told Reuters that the Dorohusk-Yahodyn crossing point had briefly stopped working after the attack around 800 meters (half a mile) from Poland, but that the crossing has since resumed operations.
Russia's Defense Ministry said it had targeted infrastructure facilitating military cargoes from Europe in Western Ukraine. Ukraine is dependent on trade and arms shipments from across the Polish, Romanian and Moldovan borders.
Russia has begun targeting Ukraine's border crossings with its Western allies in recent weeks, part of a growing campaign by both sides to erode the other's economic infrastructure more than four years into Russia's invasion.
India and China Offer to Help Broker Peace
In India, where Russian President Vladimir Putin had been attending the BRICS summit, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that both Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping had offered help brokering a peace settlement, Russian state news agency TASS reported.
Last month, at a summit in Kyrgyzstan, Modi told Putin that the war must end, one of several calls for peace by leaders of nations that have traditionally strong relations with Russia.
Last month, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev publicly told Putin that he should halt the conflict along the front line, which has remained largely static this year.
Russia has ruled that out, saying Ukraine should pull back to leave the industrialized eastern Donbas region in Moscow's hands, something Kyiv has said it will never do.
Both Brazil and China, themselves founding BRICS members, have called for a resumption of peace talks.
TASS cited Peskov as saying that Putin had informed Modi of the situation “on the ground” in Ukraine, and that Russia had not ruled out resuming three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States in October.

Ukraine Tests Automated Drone Warning System for Gas Stations
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:15:00 UTC
16:15:00 KST

Ukraine is testing an automated early warning software system to alert gas station complexes of approaching drones following an intensification of Russian aerial strikes targeting fuel distribution networks, Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi announced on Saturday, Sept. 12.
Koretskyi announced the initiative following an interagency meeting with fuel retail operators, representatives of the National Security and Defense Council (NSDC), the State Emergency Service (SES), the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and the ministries of energy, economy, finance, and infrastructure.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
The automated system tracks incoming unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and predicts flight trajectories, enabling gas stations to receive preemptive alerts and initiate safety protocols before munitions strike.
“A software solution is currently being tested that will make it possible to track the direction of drone movement and respond to threats in advance,” Koretskyi said. “The system is designed to automatically notify filling station complexes of approaching enemy UAVs.”
Koretskyi noted that following the trial phase across retail fuel networks, the government plans to scale the early warning software to other critical commercial enterprises and industrial facilities, adding that relevant ministers have been instructed to accelerate implementation.
Physical shelters and fuel logistics contingency measures
Alongside the early warning software, the government and market operators evaluated physical security enhancements for fuel distribution points.
Russian Strikes Hit Odesa High-Rise, Postal Depot, and Power Grid
Participants reviewed plans to construct additional blast-protection structures around above-ground fuel infrastructure and expand certified bomb shelters for station staff and customers.
The working group also evaluated domestic fuel supplies, transport logistics, and retail pricing pressures. Koretskyi noted that escalating conflict in the Middle East and international transit disruptions have exerted upward pressure on global crude benchmarks, directly influencing domestic retail fuel markets.
To ensure steady domestic supply lines, officials agreed on operational measures to prioritize rail freight for petroleum products and streamline customs clearance protocols for cross-border fuel tanker trucks, mirroring emergency deregulation measures enacted in 2022.
Escalating drone strikes on Kyiv filling stations
The technological and logistical measures follow consecutive deadly Russian drone strikes targeting retail filling stations in the Ukrainian capital.
On Friday morning, Sept. 11, Russian strike drones attacked two filling stations operated by state-owned oil company Ukrnafta in Kyiv, killing two people and injuring four others.
One drone struck a station in the Dniprovskyi district, while a second station in the Obolonskyi district was hit twice in succession. Six people were initially injured across the capital, with two hospitalized victims subsequently succumbing to their wounds.
The Friday assault followed an attack on Thursday, Sept. 10, when a Russian jet-powered drone struck an Ukrnafta station in Kyiv’s Holosiivskyi district, injuring four people and igniting fires that damaged adjacent commercial buildings, parked vehicles, and a public transit stop.

Support for Friedrich Merz is declining among Germans and fellow party members. Markus Söder is gaining popularity in the CDU, while Boris Pistorius is leading in the SPD.
The level of support for German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has weakened not only among the population but also within the political force he represents. BILD reports, according to UNN.
Details
The chancellor is experiencing a decline in popularity: only 14 percent of Germans consider Friedrich Merz worthy of holding the office, while support for him is weakening even within his own party. At the same time, CSU leader Markus Söder is gaining momentum in the "Christian Democratic Union" and overshadowing Merz

In particular, Lars Klingbeil is losing support, while Defense Minister Boris Pistorius leads in popularity ratings. China's Xi calls on BRICS, partner countries to keep supply chains ‘stable, unimpeded’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:07:35 UTC
16:07:35 KST

Saadet Gokce
13 September 2026•Update: 13 September 2026
- China to take lead in establishing AI open-source zone for BRICS, promoting digital industry cloud platform for bloc's countries
Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sunday called on expanded BRICS members and partner countries to keep industrial and supply chains "stable and unimpeded" amid disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz due to the US-Iran war.
 
"Greater BRICS" should leverage strengths in being rooted in emerging markets and connected with the Global South, uphold openness and cooperation for "mutual benefit and win-win outcomes," keep industrial and supply chains "stable and unimpeded," and foster integrated markets, Xi said during the final day of the two-day 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, according to state-run news agency Xinhua.
 
He was speaking at an open session titled "Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth."
 
The Chinese president said that the Global South has become a "key force driving the world toward multipolarity," and urged countries to uphold multilateralism and international rule of law.
 
Xi added that the international rules should be jointly written by all, and that "might makes right" logic should have been discarded long ago.
 
The Global South countries should "uphold authority and role of the UN," while supporting reforms to improve the efficiency of multilateral institutions, Xi said.
 
Xi called for improving international financial architecture, enhancing representation and say of developing countries, as well as a WTO reform in the “right direction.”
 
"China will further advance voluntary and unilateral opening-up," he added.
 
He urged support for the operation and development of the New Development Bank, as well as stronger Global South cooperation.
 
The Global South should accelerate efforts to establish a global AI governance framework based on broad consensus, Xi said, adding that China would take the lead in establishing an AI open-source zone for BRICS and promoting a digital industry cloud platform for BRICS countries.
 
The Chinese president also called on the "greater BRICS" to upgrade traditional industries, develop emerging sectors, and make forward-looking plans for future industries, foster integrated markets and "lay a solid foundation for practical cooperation."
 
He also proposed initiatives on science and technology talent development, smart manufacturing, digital industry, trade and investment facilitation, and "open and inclusive" AI, as well as a BRICS alliance for engineer training.
 
Xi additionally proposed building special economic zones partnership of BRICS countries.
 
China will host the BRICS Services Trade Forum in 2027, he also said, while Beijing is also due to host the bloc's annual summit next year.
